# Parallel Review Plan

Receive plan artifacts as read-only input and produce structured findings conforming to `review-findings.schema.json`. Designed for vendor-diverse dispatch — any LLM agent can execute this skill.

## Arguments

`$ARGUMENTS` - OpenSpec change-id to review (e.g., "add-user-authentication")

Optional flags:
- `--adversarial` — Use adversarial review mode: challenges design decisions instead of standard review

## Prerequisites

- OpenSpec proposal exists at `openspec/changes/<change-id>/`
- Proposal has been generated by `/parallel-plan-feature` or `/linear-plan-feature`

## Provider-Neutral Dispatch

Plan review uses the provider-neutral dispatch adapter/configuration path as
the canonical cross-provider mechanism. Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Grok,
and Pi are first-class reviewers when configured; provider-specific CLI or
harness details stay inside their adapters.

## Input (Read-Only)

The reviewer receives these artifacts as context but MUST NOT modify them:

- `openspec/changes/<change-id>/proposal.md`
- `openspec/changes/<change-id>/design.md`
- `openspec/changes/<change-id>/tasks.md`
- `openspec/changes/<change-id>/specs/**/spec.md`
- `openspec/changes/<change-id>/contracts/` (if present)
- `openspec/changes/<change-id>/work-packages.yaml` (if present)

## Eight-Axis Finding Schema

Every finding produced by this skill MUST be classified into BOTH dimensions below. The JSON Schema at `openspec/schemas/review-findings.schema.json` enforces both fields as `required` — output that omits either is rejected by the validator in Step 4.

### Eight Axes (the `axis` field)

Five axes adopted from the `code-review-and-quality` reference skill, plus three fitness-function axes. Pick exactly one:

| Axis | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `correctness` | Does the plan, when implemented, produce the right answer? Bugs, off-by-one, missing requirements, ambiguous SHALL clauses. |
| `readability` | Will a future reader understand intent? Naming, structure, spec clarity, ambiguous prose. |
| `architecture` | Does the design fit the system? Module boundaries, layering, coupling, dependency direction, contract shape. |
| `security` | Does the plan introduce or fail to prevent security risk? Auth gaps, input-validation holes, secret handling, OWASP categories. |
| `performance` | Will the implementation be fast and scalable enough? N+1, unbounded queries, missing pagination, hot-path allocations. |
| `observability` | Can the running system be understood from the outside? Missing logs/metrics/traces, unactionable errors, no way to detect the failure mode the plan introduces. |
| `resilience` | Does it degrade safely? Missing retries/timeouts/backoff, unbounded blast radius, no fallback, undefined partial-failure behavior. |
| `compatibility` | Does it stay compatible with what already exists? Breaking API/schema/CLI changes, missing migration path, version or platform assumptions. |

The legacy `type` enum (`spec_gap`, `contract_mismatch`, etc. — see Step 3) is preserved for backward compatibility; `axis` is the new mandatory categorization that all reviewers — human or vendor — must agree on.

### Five Severity Prefixes (the `severity` field)

Every finding's `description` MUST begin with one of these markers. The `severity` enum value MUST match the prefix.

| Prefix | Severity value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Critical` | `critical` | Blocks merge. Must be fixed before implementation begins (or before the PR merges). |
| `Nit` | `nit` | Should fix but does not block. Quality, naming, minor structure. |
| `Optional` | `optional` | Consider it. Author may accept or reject without further discussion. |
| `FYI` | `fyi` | Informational. Surfaces context the author may not have known; no action required. |
| `none` | `none` | Positive observation. Names what the plan got right so good patterns survive review. |

Example finding (note prefix and matching `severity`):

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "axis": "security",
  "severity": "critical",
  "type": "security",
  "criticality": "high",
  "description": "Critical: Requirement R3 admits unauthenticated DELETE on /v1/users/{id} — missing auth precondition.",
  "resolution": "Add a SHALL clause requiring an authenticated session with role=admin before the DELETE handler executes.",
  "disposition": "fix"
}
```

Reviewers MUST NOT collapse multiple severities onto one finding (split them). Reviewers MUST NOT use a severity that contradicts the `disposition` (e.g., `severity: critical` with `disposition: accept` is incoherent — escalate instead).

## Steps

### 1. Load Review Context

Read all plan artifacts listed above. Build a mental model of:
- What the feature does (proposal.md)
- How it will be built (design.md)
- What requirements it satisfies (specs/)
- How work is decomposed (tasks.md, work-packages.yaml)

### 2. Review Checklist

Evaluate the plan against these dimensions:

#### Specification Completeness
- [ ] All requirements use SHALL/MUST language
- [ ] Requirements are testable and verifiable
- [ ] No ambiguous or vague terms

#### Contract Consistency
- [ ] OpenAPI schemas match spec requirements
- [ ] Database schemas support all declared operations
- [ ] Event schemas cover all async flows
- [ ] Generated types match OpenAPI definitions

#### Architecture Alignment
- [ ] Design follows existing codebase patterns
- [ ] No unnecessary dependencies introduced
- [ ] Error handling strategy is complete
- [ ] Migration path is reversible

#### Security Review
- [ ] Input validation at system boundaries
- [ ] Authentication/authorization for new endpoints
- [ ] No secrets in configuration or code
- [ ] OWASP top-10 considerations addressed

#### Performance Review
- [ ] No unbounded queries or loops in design
- [ ] List operations have pagination or size limits
- [ ] Synchronous operations that should be async are identified
- [ ] Caching strategy defined for hot paths (if applicable)
- [ ] Rate limiting considered for public endpoints

#### Observability Review
- [ ] Monitoring requirements defined for new services/endpoints
- [ ] Structured logging requirements for key operations
- [ ] Alerting criteria specified for failure conditions
- [ ] Health/readiness endpoint requirements for new services

#### Compatibility Review
- [ ] Breaking changes to existing APIs are identified and justified
- [ ] Data migration plan is reversible (rollback path exists)
- [ ] Consumer impact analysis for changed interfaces
- [ ] Deprecation notices for removed or changed APIs

#### Resilience Review
- [ ] Retry/timeout/fallback requirements for external dependencies
- [ ] Failure mode analysis for critical paths
- [ ] Idempotency requirements for operations that may be retried
- [ ] Graceful degradation strategy when dependencies are unavailable

#### Work Package Validity (if work-packages.yaml exists)
- [ ] DAG has no cycles
- [ ] Parallel packages have non-overlapping write scopes
- [ ] Lock keys follow canonicalization rules
- [ ] Verification steps are appropriate for each package tier
- [ ] Integration package depends on all implementation packages

### 3. Produce Findings

Generate findings as a JSON array conforming to `review-findings.schema.json`:

```json
{
  "review_type": "plan",
  "target": "<change-id>",
  "reviewer_vendor": "<model-name>",
  "findings": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "type": "spec_gap",
      "criticality": "high",
      "description": "Requirement R3 lacks error handling specification for 429 rate limit responses",
      "resolution": "Add a requirement specifying retry-after header handling",
      "disposition": "fix"
    }
  ]
}
```

#### Finding Types
- `spec_gap` — Missing or incomplete requirements
- `contract_mismatch` — Inconsistency between contracts and specs
- `architecture` — Design pattern or structural concern
- `security` — Security vulnerability or missing protection
- `performance` — Potential performance issue
- `style` — Code style or convention violation
- `correctness` — Logical error in the plan
- `observability` — Missing monitoring, logging, or alerting requirements
- `compatibility` — Breaking change to existing API or missing migration plan
- `resilience` — Missing retry, timeout, or fallback requirements

#### Dispositions
- `fix` — Author should fix before implementation
- `regenerate` — Artifact needs regeneration (e.g., contract schema mismatch)
- `accept` — Minor issue, acceptable as-is
- `escalate` — Requires human decision or cross-team coordination

### 4. Validate Output

Validate the findings JSON against `openspec/schemas/review-findings.schema.json`:

```bash
# Quick validation
python3 -c "
import json, jsonschema
schema = json.load(open('openspec/schemas/review-findings.schema.json'))
findings = json.load(open('<findings-output-path>'))
jsonschema.validate(findings, schema)
print('Valid')
"
```

### 5. Submit Findings

Write findings to `openspec/changes/<change-id>/review-findings-plan.json`.

If `CAN_HANDOFF=true`, write a review handoff with:
- Summary of critical/high findings
- Overall disposition recommendation (proceed/revise/block)

### 6. Dispatch Multi-Vendor Reviews

After writing your own findings, dispatch reviews to other vendor CLIs and synthesize consensus.

**Write the review prompt** to `openspec/changes/<change-id>/reviews/review-prompt.md` — include instructions to read the plan artifacts and output only valid JSON conforming to `review-findings.schema.json`. The required-field list and enums MUST come from `review_findings_schema.prompt_contract()` / `prompt_contract_block()` — do not hand-copy the field list.

**Adversarial mode**: If `--adversarial` flag was passed, wrap the review prompt with adversarial framing before dispatch:

```python
from adversarial_prompt import wrap_adversarial
prompt = wrap_adversarial(prompt)  # Prepends contrarian persona instructions
```

The dispatch still uses `--mode review` (unchanged) — only the prompt content differs. Adversarial findings flow through the same consensus pipeline with equal weight (Design Decision D1).

**Dispatch to other vendors** (excluding the current agent's vendor):

```bash
python3 "<skill-base-dir>/../parallel-infrastructure/scripts/review_dispatcher.py" \
  --review-type plan \
  --mode review \
  --prompt-file "openspec/changes/<change-id>/reviews/review-prompt.md" \
  --cwd "$(pwd)" \
  --output-dir "openspec/changes/<change-id>/reviews" \
  --exclude-vendor claude_code \
  --timeout 600
```

This dispatches to all available vendors configured in `agents.yaml` with `cli` sections. Each vendor runs independently and writes findings to `reviews/findings-<vendor>-plan.json`.

**Agent discovery resolution chain**: An explicit `--agents-yaml` wins. Otherwise the dispatcher searches from the reviewed `--cwd` for checkout-local `agent-coordinator/agents.yaml`, then tries the configured coordination MCP/HTTP roster, and finally the process/global disk fallback. SDK-only coordinator rosters count as configured and are not discarded. Dispatch, `--check-vendors`, and `--list-agents` use this same resolver. Use `--list-agents --cwd <reviewed-checkout>` to verify the exact roster.

**Troubleshooting dispatch failures**: Run `python3 <script> --list-agents` to verify agent discovery. Common issues: (1) `~/.claude.json` has no `mcpServers.coordination` entry — run `/setup-coordinator`, (2) async/remote agents may time out — local agents are more reliable, (3) some vendors may return non-JSON output — check `review-manifest.json` for error details.

**Synthesize consensus** from all findings (yours + vendor results):

```bash
python3 "<skill-base-dir>/../parallel-infrastructure/scripts/consensus_synthesizer.py" \
  --review-type plan \
  --target "<change-id>" \
  --findings "openspec/changes/<change-id>/review-findings-plan.json" \
             "openspec/changes/<change-id>/reviews/findings-"*"-plan.json" \
  --output "openspec/changes/<change-id>/reviews/consensus-plan.json"
```

**Present consensus summary** to the user:
- Confirmed findings (2+ vendors agree) — high confidence, may block
- Unconfirmed findings (single vendor) — lower confidence, warnings
- Disagreements (vendors disagree on disposition) — escalate to human

If no other vendors are available (CLIs not installed), skip this step and proceed with single-vendor findings only.

## Output

- `openspec/changes/<change-id>/review-findings-plan.json` — your findings
- `openspec/changes/<change-id>/reviews/findings-<vendor>-plan.json` — per-vendor findings
- `openspec/changes/<change-id>/reviews/consensus-plan.json` — synthesized consensus
- `openspec/changes/<change-id>/reviews/review-manifest.json` — dispatch metadata

## Design for Vendor Diversity

This skill is intentionally simple and self-contained so it can be dispatched to any LLM agent:
- No coordinator dependencies required
- All input is file-based (read-only)
- Output is a single JSON file with a well-defined schema
- No side effects (no git commits, no lock acquisition)

When this skill is dispatched *to* another vendor by the orchestrator, only Steps 1-5 run (the vendor produces findings). Step 6 (multi-vendor dispatch) only runs when this skill is the *primary* reviewer — i.e., when invoked directly by the user or the orchestrating agent.

## Common Rationalizations

| Rationalization | Why it's wrong |
|---|---|
| "I only found one issue, so I'll skip the axis/severity classification — the description is enough" | The schema rejects findings without `axis` and `severity`; cross-vendor consensus relies on these fields to match equivalent findings. Skipping = the dispatcher discards your review. |
| "This finding spans two axes — I'll just pick one" | Pick the dominant axis and split the rest into separate findings. Mashing two axes into one description means consensus matching cannot deduplicate against another vendor who split them. |
| "The plan looks fine — I'll just emit zero findings" | A review with zero findings is suspicious. At minimum, emit `severity: none` positive observations naming what the plan got right; this signals the review actually happened rather than timed out. |
| "The orchestrator will catch contradictions between `severity` and `disposition`" | It won't — the orchestrator routes by `disposition`. Inconsistent severity/disposition pairs survive into the consensus and confuse downstream automation. Make them coherent at write time. |

## Red Flags

- A `review-findings-plan.json` file with findings that lack the `axis` field — the schema validation step (Step 4) was skipped or its output ignored.
- Every finding has the same severity (e.g., everything is `Critical`). A real review covers a spectrum; uniform severity means the reviewer wasn't actually grading.
- Description prose does NOT start with the matching severity prefix (`Critical:` / `Nit:` / `Optional:` / `FYI:` / nothing-for-`none`). The prefix is the human-readable signal; if it disagrees with the enum value, the reviewer wrote the JSON without re-reading the prose.
- A `security`-axis finding with `disposition: accept`. Security findings are never silently accepted; if the risk is real, the disposition must be `fix` or `escalate`.
- Findings reference file paths or line ranges that don't exist in the plan artifacts (proposal/design/specs). The reviewer hallucinated context.

## Verification

1. Run the JSON Schema validator from Step 4 and confirm `Valid` — this proves `axis` and `severity` are present on every finding.
2. Spot-check 3 findings: confirm the `description` text begins with the prefix matching the `severity` enum value (e.g., `severity: critical` ↔ description starts with `Critical:`).
3. Confirm at least two different `axis` values appear across the findings array (a single-axis review missed the other seven dimensions of the schema).
4. Confirm `disposition` is coherent with `severity`: `critical`/`nit` → `fix`; `optional`/`fyi` → `accept`; `none` → `accept`; mismatches must be `escalate` with a justification in `resolution`.
5. Confirm `reviewer_vendor` is populated — anonymous findings cannot participate in consensus.

    38	- Lane, task, and roadmap-policy feasibility is resolved before the existing dg-00
    39	  utility scorer runs; no second resolver or model call is introduced.
    40	- Every lane/model association comes from dg-01's exact catalog projection. Name
    41	  suffixes, publisher guesses, and fuzzy model matching are forbidden.
    42	- Changing validated `routing.yaml` rules changes deterministic decisions without code
    43	  edits, and the policy version/checksum is recorded.
    44	- Coordinator-side decisions are durably recorded in both routing decision storage and
    45	  coordinator audit. Local fallback decisions declare that durable audit was unavailable.
    46	- The dg-00 fallback contract remains byte-for-byte equal for existing
    47	  `resolve_archetype_for_phase` callers when adaptive routing is disabled, fails, or
    48	  times out.
    49	
    50	## Non-goals
    51	
    52	- No `/route/task` endpoint or parallel scoring implementation.
    53	- No per-dispatch-mode isolation override or precedence ladder (dg-05).
    54	- No orchestrator call-site wiring, redispatch, or loop-control changes (dg-06).
    55	- No operating-system isolation enforcement (dg-07).
    56	- No duplicate price table, roster, health cache, or inferred vendor identity.

     1	## ADDED Requirements
     2	
     3	### Requirement: One additive routing surface
     4	
     5	The coordinator SHALL extend `POST /routing/select_model` and its
     6	`select_model_for_task` MCP mirror with task-profile and assignment fields, and SHALL NOT
     7	add a second task-routing endpoint or scoring path.
     8	
     9	#### Scenario: Existing HTTP and MCP surfaces stay aligned
    10	
    11	- **WHEN** the same valid task-routing request is submitted through HTTP and direct MCP
    12	- **THEN** both surfaces SHALL validate the same typed profile and return the same
    13	  assignment/provenance shape
    14	- **AND** no `POST /route/task` route SHALL be registered.
    15	
    16	#### Scenario: Legacy caller remains compatible
    17	
    18	- **WHEN** a caller sends only the dg-00 `task_signals.archetype` field
    19	- **THEN** the request SHALL remain valid
    20	- **AND** newly added input and output fields SHALL use additive defaults.
    21	
    22	### Requirement: Typed task-routing profile
    23	
    24	The request SHALL type phase/archetype, expected duration, scope, interactivity, secret
    25	need, parallelism, repository shape, roadmap policy, and optional location, isolation,
    26	and dispatch-mode constraints at the HTTP/MCP boundary.
    27	
    28	#### Scenario: Invalid profile is rejected at the boundary
    29	
    30	- **WHEN** a task profile contains an invalid enum, negative duration, non-positive
    31	  parallelism, or malformed policy constraint
    32	- **THEN** HTTP SHALL return 422
    33	- **AND** direct MCP SHALL return the existing matching validation-error envelope.
    34	
    35	#### Scenario: Config rules consume typed signals
    36	
    37	- **WHEN** a validated `routing.yaml` rule matches a task-profile field
    38	- **THEN** its configured location, isolation, or dispatch-mode constraint SHALL be
    39	  applied deterministically
    40	- **AND** the matching rule ID SHALL be recorded in decision provenance.
    41	
    42	### Requirement: Registry-backed feasibility precedes utility
    43	
    44	The router SHALL consume `VendorRegistryService` in process and remove infeasible
    45	lane/model assignments before invoking the existing dg-00 utility scorer.
    46	
    47	#### Scenario: Exact lane and catalog association
    48	
    49	- **WHEN** a registry lane projects a catalog model
    50	- **THEN** routing SHALL associate it only by the exact projected catalog vendor, model,
    51	  and endpoint-kind identity
    52	- **AND** SHALL NOT infer association from agent ID suffixes, publisher names, or fuzzy
    53	  model strings.
    54	
    55	#### Scenario: Infeasible assignment cannot win
    56	
    57	- **WHEN** a lane is unavailable, rate limited, lacks the archetype or dispatch mode, or
    58	  violates location, isolation, or roadmap-policy constraints
    59	- **THEN** the lane/model assignment SHALL be excluded before dg-00 utility scoring
    60	- **AND** the exclusion SHALL carry a machine-readable reason.
    61	
    62	#### Scenario: Feasible assignments retain dg-00 ranking
    63	
    64	- **WHEN** two or more lane/model assignments remain feasible
    65	- **THEN** their quality, cost, latency, headroom, and exploration ranking SHALL be
    66	  produced by the existing dg-00 scorer without a second utility function.
    67	
    68	### Requirement: Versioned deterministic routing policy
    69	
    70	Routing dimension rules SHALL be loaded from a schema-validated `routing.yaml` carrying
    71	an explicit schema version and policy version.
    72	
    73	#### Scenario: Policy edit changes a decision
    74	
    75	- **WHEN** a test changes a valid rule or phase default in `routing.yaml`
    76	- **THEN** the resulting assignment SHALL change without a Python code edit
    77	- **AND** repeated evaluation of the same profile, registry snapshot, catalog snapshot,
    78	  and policy SHALL produce the same ordered candidates when exploration is disabled.
    79	
    80	#### Scenario: Invalid policy fails loud
    81	
    82	- **WHEN** `routing.yaml` contains an unknown field, unsupported schema version, invalid
    83	  enum, duplicate rule ID, or reference to an unconfigured phase default
    84	- **THEN** policy loading SHALL fail before routing a task
    85	- **AND** SHALL NOT silently substitute permissive defaults.
    86	
    87	### Requirement: Additive assignment and provenance
    88	
    89	Every selected candidate SHALL expose exact lane assignment fields and every persisted
    90	decision SHALL retain the task profile, policy version/checksum, matched rules, excluded
    91	assignments, and source.
    92	
    93	#### Scenario: Coordinator decision is durable and auditable
    94	
    95	- **WHEN** the coordinator returns a routing decision
    96	- **THEN** the same decision ID and assignment SHALL be written to `routing_decisions`
    97	- **AND** a durable coordinator audit event SHALL record sanitized request,
    98	  assignment, policy provenance, and success.
    99	
   100	#### Scenario: Alternative candidates retain lane identity
   101	
   102	- **WHEN** feasible alternatives are returned
   103	- **THEN** each alternative SHALL retain its own exact `agent_id`, vendor type,
   104	  location, isolation, dispatch mode, model, and endpoint kind.
   105	
   106	### Requirement: Honest local fallback
   107	
   108	A coordinator-unreachable client path SHALL derive a deterministic assignment only from
   109	the checkout's validated `routing.yaml`, `agents.yaml`, archetype model map, and caller's
   110	static model/provider inputs.
   111	
   112	#### Scenario: Coordinator is unreachable
   113	
   114	- **WHEN** the coordinator routing operation times out or is unreachable
   115	- **THEN** the local helper SHALL return the normal assignment shape with
   116	  `fallback=true`, `source=local-static`, and `durable_audit=false`
   117	- **AND** SHALL NOT embed a roster, synthesize live availability, or claim a coordinator
   118	  audit record exists.
   119	
   120	#### Scenario: Existing static fallback equality is preserved
   121	
   122	- **WHEN** existing `resolve_archetype_for_phase` adaptive routing is disabled, fails,
   123	  returns malformed data, or exceeds its bounded timeout
   124	- **THEN** the returned `ResolvedArchetype` SHALL equal the dg-00 static result exactly.

 succeeded in 0ms:
     1	# Design: extend routing to vendor × location × isolation × dispatch mode
     2	
     3	## D1 — Extend one resolver and one public operation
     4	
     5	DG-04 extends the dg-00 `RoutingService.select_model()` pipeline, HTTP
     6	`POST /routing/select_model`, and MCP `select_model_for_task`. It does not add
     7	`POST /route/task`, a second score function, or a second routing decision store.
     8	The existing `selected.vendor/model/endpoint_kind` meaning remains observable and
     9	unchanged; assignment and provenance are additive fields.
    10	
    11	## D2 — Preserve compatibility with an optional strict profile
    12	
    13	Legacy `task_signals` remains accepted with its current permissive extra-field
    14	behavior because existing phase callers send fields such as `write_allow`. A new
    15	optional `routing_profile` is strict (`extra=forbid`) and types:
    16	
    17	- expected duration seconds;
    18	- scope category (`read-only|bounded-write|broad-write`);
    19	- interactivity (`interactive|headless`);
    20	- secret need category (`none|brokered|direct`), never a secret value;
    21	- positive parallelism;
    22	- repository shape (`single-package|monorepo|unknown`);
    23	- roadmap-policy constraints (allowed/excluded lane/vendor/location sets);
    24	- optional required location, isolation, and dispatch mode.
    25	
    26	Pydantic validates the external boundary and FastAPI/MCP share the same request model.
    27	New response objects are optional-with-default for legacy validation but are always
    28	populated by a successful DG-04 service decision.
    29	
    30	## D3 — Rules are ordered, typed, and versioned
    31	
    32	`agent-coordinator/routing.yaml` carries `schema_version`, `policy_version`,
    33	phase defaults, ordered first-match rules, and a fallback-dimension table. A dedicated
    34	loader validates unknown fields, duplicate IDs, enum values, ranges, and phase defaults,
    35	then records a SHA-256 checksum of canonical file bytes.
    36	
    37	Each rule has a typed `when` predicate over the profile and a typed `set` block for
    38	location, isolation, and dispatch mode. Explicit request constraints take precedence;
    39	otherwise the first matching rule supplies a dimension and phase/default values fill the
    40	remainder. Rules narrow feasibility and never add a second utility score. Changing a
    41	rule therefore changes the feasible assignment set without code edits.
    42	
    43	The Docker image copies the file beside `agents.yaml` and the loader resolves it from
    44	`ROUTING_CONFIG` or the package root, never the process working directory.
    45	
    46	## D4 — DG-01 is the only lane source and joins are exact
    47	
    48	`RoutingService` injects/loads `VendorRegistryService` in process and requests all
    49	lanes without `available_only` prefiltering so exclusion provenance is retained. For
    50	each lane it consumes dg-01's projected catalog models. It forms an assignment only when
    51	the catalog candidate identity exactly equals the projection key:
    52	
    53	`(catalog_vendor, model, endpoint_kind, base_url)`.
    54	
    55	`base_url` and additive lane identity travel through `CandidateInput` and
    56	`ScoredCandidate`. Agent-name suffixes, provider/publisher guesses, substring matches,
    57	and fuzzy model names are forbidden. Missing or ambiguous projections remain explicit
    58	registry misses and never become routable candidates.
    59	
    60	## D5 — Feasibility precedes DG-00 utility
    61	
    62	For each exact lane/model pair, pure feasibility checks apply in deterministic order:
    63	
    64	1. live lane availability and lane/model rate limits;
    65	2. dispatchability, archetype, and requested/default dispatch mode;
    66	3. explicit/configured location and isolation constraints;
    67	4. roadmap-policy allow/exclude sets;
    68	5. catalog availability and dg-00 modality/quota constraints.
    69	
    70	Reasons are machine-readable and sanitized. Only feasible lane/model candidates enter
    71	the existing `score_and_rank`; DG-04 does not duplicate quality, posterior, cost,
    72	latency, headroom, or exploration math. Multiple lanes may project the same catalog
    73	model, so the final stable order is `(-score, agent_id, catalog identity)`.
    74	
    75	## D6 — Assignment and provenance are additive
    76	
    77	A successful response adds top-level:
    78	
    79	- `assignment`: exact `agent_id`, `vendor_type`, `policy_vendor`,
    80	  `catalog_vendor`, location, isolation, dispatch mode, model, endpoint kind, and base
    81	  URL;
    82	- `provenance`: source (`coordinator` or `local-static`), policy version/checksum,
    83	  matched rule IDs, rationale, persistence flag, durable-audit flag, and exact
    84	  lane/catalog key.
    85	
    86	Alternatives retain their own lane assignment rather than losing identity after model
    87	scoring. Existing selected-candidate fields remain intact for older consumers.
    88	
    89	## D7 — Durable routing record is authoritative; audit event is linked
    90	
    91	The existing `routing_decisions` row is the authoritative durable routing audit. Its
    92	JSONB request/selected/alternatives/excluded fields accept additive assignment and
    93	provenance, so no schema migration is required.
    94	
    95	After that row is inserted, DG-04 emits a sanitized `routing_decision` audit-log event
    96	that links only the decision ID, selected agent/model, policy version, and source. The
    97	write uses an awaited durable audit operation and fails the request if durability cannot
    98	be established; fire-and-forget acceptance is insufficient. The generic audit event is
    99	an index/link, not a second source of routing truth.
   100	
   101	No raw secret, environment value, prompt, or unbounded path list enters either record;
   102	only typed secret-need and scope categories are retained.
   103	
   104	## D8 — Local fallback is configuration-derived and honest
   105	
   106	A skills-side bridge/helper may fall back only after transport timeout/unreachability. It
   107	loads the checkout's validated `routing.yaml`, `agents.yaml`, and archetype model map,
   108	then combines the caller's already-resolved static provider/model with the fallback
   109	dimension order. It never embeds a roster, fabricates availability, or performs fuzzy
   110	association.
   111	
   112	The response has the normal assignment shape plus `fallback=true`,
   113	`source=local-static`, `persisted=false`, `durable_audit=false`, and a bounded
   114	failure reason. A local UUID is explicitly not retrievable from coordinator decision
   115	storage.
   116	
   117	The existing `resolve_archetype_for_phase` fallback is not rewritten: disabled,
   118	failure, malformed-response, and timeout paths still return the exact dg-00 static
   119	`ResolvedArchetype` object with no added reasons or fields.
   120	
   121	## D9 — DG-05/DG-06 boundaries remain closed
   122	
   123	DG-04 carries the lane's current configured isolation as data and may filter an explicit
   124	request. It does not define per-mode overrides, the isolation precedence ladder, or
   125	enforcement; DG-05 owns that contract. It does not call routing before `dispatch_fn`,
   126	change `phase_agent.py`, redispatch work, or add loop caps; DG-06 owns obedience.
   127	No sandbox is launched; DG-07 owns enforcement.
   128	
   129	## D10 — Test-first packages and validation
   130	
   131	Contract/config tests fail first, followed by pure policy/association tests, then service
   132	and transport/fallback tests. PostgreSQL coverage proves the additive JSONB decision
   133	round trip and durable audit link. Full coordinator and affected skills suites, Ruff,
   134	strict mypy, strict OpenSpec, work-package DAG/scope checks, configured vendor-panel
   135	plan/implementation convergence, stacked PR CI, and exact static-fallback regression
   136	must all pass before roadmap reconciliation.
   137	
   138	Framework-specific implementation follows the installed FastAPI/Pydantic versions and
   139	their official model/response documentation:
   140	https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/models/ and
   141	https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/response-model/.

Adaptive Roadmap Execution\n\nThe system SHALL provide an `autopilot-roadmap` workflow that executes roadmap items iteratively and updates pending items using implementation evidence. When an item fails, `CheckpointManager.fail_item(checkpoint, roadmap, item_id, reason, *, replan=False)` SHALL transition the failed item's dependents to `blocked` by default and to `replan_required` only when the failing item's outcome payload carries an explicit `replan: true` signal; the workflow SHALL NOT infer hard-versus-workaroundable from the failure text. For every item in `replan_required`, the orchestrator SHALL evaluate `Gate.REPLAN_REQUIRED` through an injected `GateEvaluator` (default `approval_gate.build_default_gate()`); on `proceed` it SHALL write a `ReplanRequest` conforming to `contracts/events/replan-request.schema.json` to `<workspace>/replan-request.json` and finish the run with status `replan_requested`; on `blocked` the items SHALL stay `replan_required`, the decision SHALL be recorded in the checkpoint, and the run SHALL continue with other ready items. The orchestrator SHALL make no LLM or network call to perform the replan itself; the host executes `/plan-roadmap --replan <roadmap-id>`.\n\n#### Scenario: Learning feedback updates remaining roadmap items\nWHEN a roadmap item completes implementation and review\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL persist a learning entry to `learnings/<item-id>.md` conforming to `contracts/learning-log.schema.json`\nAND it SHALL update the root `learning-log.md` index with a one-line summary\nAND before the next item begins it SHALL ingest prior learning entries (direct dependencies + most recent 3)\nAND it SHALL update pending item recommendations accordingly.\n\n#### Scenario: Resume from persisted checkpoint after interruption\nWHEN roadmap execution stops before completion\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL resume from the last successful checkpoint conforming to `contracts/checkpoint.schema.json`\nAND it SHALL skip phases already marked complete unless forced by user input.\n\n#### Scenario: Abort item execution when prerequisite roadmap dependency is incomplete\nWHEN a roadmap item is selected for execution\nAND one or more of its dependency items are not complete\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL block execution of that item\nAND it SHALL emit a dependency-blocked status with missing dependency IDs.\n\n#### Scenario: Handle individual roadmap item implementation failure\nWHEN a roadmap item fails implementation (tests fail, review rejects, or design dead-end)\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL mark the item as `failed` in `roadmap.yaml` with a structured failure reason\nAND it SHALL persist a learning entry recording the failure details, root cause, and recommendations\nAND it SHALL transition dependent items in `approved` or `candidate` status to `blocked`\nAND it SHALL proceed to the next eligible item rather than halting the entire roadmap.\n\n#### Scenario: Explicit replan signal produces replan_required\nWHEN a roadmap item fails and its outcome payload contains `replan: true`\nTHEN `fail_item(..., replan=True)` SHALL transition dependents in `approved` or `candidate` status to `replan_required` instead of `blocked`\nAND each such dependent SHALL record the failed item id in `blocked_by`\nAND the failed item itself SHALL still be marked `failed`.\n\n#### Scenario: Replan gate proceeds and emits a request\nWHEN at least one item is in `replan_required` after a failure is recorded\nAND `Gate.REPLAN_REQUIRED` evaluates to `proceed`\nTHEN the orchestrator SHALL write `<workspace>/replan-request.json` listing the `replan_required` item ids, the failed item id, and the gate decision\nAND the run summary status SHALL be `replan_requested`\nAND no item in `replan_required` SHALL be dispatched.\n\n#### Scenario: Replan gate blocked leaves items parked\nWHEN `Gate.REPLAN_REQUIRED` evaluates to `blocked` (posture `block`, timeout default block, or coordinator unreachable)\nTHEN no `replan-request.json` SHALL be written\nAND the affected items SHALL remain `replan_required`\nAND the decision SHALL be persisted in the checkpoint's `gate_decisions`\nAND the orchestrator SHALL continue with other ready items.\n\n#### Scenario: Orchestrator never performs the replan itself\nWHEN a replan request is emitted\nTHEN `skills/autopilot-roadmap/scripts/` SHALL contain no import of an LLM SDK and no network call to perform re-decomposition\nAND the host-assisted invariant test SHALL continue to pass.\n\n### Requirement: Usage-Limit-Aware Multi-Vendor Scheduling\n\nThe system SHALL apply explicit policy when vendor session/rate limits are encountered during roadmap execution.\n\n#### Scenario: Wait policy selected under budget constraints\nWHEN the preferred vendor hits a usage/session limit\nAND artifact writers SHALL sanitize content before persisting to prevent secret exposure in durable, potentially committed state.\n\n#### Scenario: Redact sensitive content from learning entries\nWHEN **AND** a crash after preparation loses agent launch work rather than losing the identity of potentially running work\n\n#### Scenario: Resume with an unresolved attempt\n- **WHEN** a fresh supervisor state before deciding whether work launched\n- **AND** pre-go stale claims may be reclaimed by generation compare-and-swap; after go, takeover requires positive task-death evidence, and unknown liveness becomes non-resumable quarantine\n\n#### Scenario: Reconcile lease crash windows\n- **WHEN** a crash occurs before marker creation, after marker but before Autopilot entry, before host acknowledgement, or while a child is active\n- **THEN** the generation-specific ack/go barrier prevents Autopilot entry before durable handle acknowledgement, while markers, heartbeats, handle status, exact worktree loop-state, and terminal handoff/result evidence classify the generation\n- **AND** a pre-go expired claim may be reclaimed safely, but a post-go generation may be reclaimed only after positive task-death evidence; mere absence or expiry enters quarantine\n- **AND** duplicate owners, active-lease token reuse, and stale owners that fail compare-and-swap are refused\n\n#### Scenario: Resume an authorized parked attempt\n- **WHEN** the supervise gate router supplies an `approval_ref` of the form `gate-decision:<decision_id>` for a `pending_gate` or `policy_pause` parked dispatch\n- `policy_pause`), and a matching `dispatch_id`, then compare-and-swaps parked to prepared, increments the lease generation, and emits one continuation with the same dispatch ID, attempt, token, worktree, and loop-state\n- **AND** a reference that does not resolve, resolves to a `blocked` decision, or names a different gate or dispatch is rejected without mutating the attempt\n- **AND** the duplicate Autopilot entry occurs\n- **AND** approval-gate resume is forbidden until reconciliation positively proves the prior task dead or terminal\n\n### Requirement: Roadmap items are refined before they are implemented\n\nAn item advanced to by the roadmap runtime SHALL enter the planning phase, so that its preliminary scaffold is refined using what was learned implementing its dependencies before any implementation begins.\n\nRoadmap items are planned one at a time rather than all at once precisely so that later items benefit from earlier ones. Advancing straight into implementation spends that opportunity and implements against a scaffold nobody revisited.\n\n#### Scenario: Advancing to the next item enters planning\nWHEN the roadmap runtime advances to the next ready item\nTHEN the checkpoint phase SHALL be set to planning\nAND the persisted checkpoint SHALL record that phase.\n\n#### Scenario: The refinement pass is not reported as already complete\nWHEN the roadmap runtime has just advanced to an item\nTHEN the planning phase SHALL NOT be reported as skippable for that item\nAND a refinement pass SHALL therefore run before implementation.\n\n#### Scenario: Refinement acts on the scaffold rather than an empty directory\nWHEN a refinement pass begins for a newly advanced item\nTHEN the item's change directory SHALL already contain the preliminary proposal and spec delta written at roadmap-creation time.\n\n### Requirement: Canonical Cross-Roadmap Readiness Resolution\n\nThe roadmap runtime SHALL expose a read-only repository-wide resolver that uses roadmap definitions plus canonical checkpoint state to emit one globally ranked ready-now list. Its JSON output MUST contain a SHA-256 `source_fingerprint` over canonical readiness-relevant input, a content-consistency `stale` signal, and bounded diagnostics. A downstream projection can detect staleness by comparing its stored source fingerprint with a newly resolved fingerprint. implementable OpenSpec change\nTHEN `plan-roadmap` SHALL merge them with adjacent items\nAND it SHALL record the merge rationale in the merged item's description.\n\n#### Scenario: Split oversized dependents that are not in a preserved status)\nAND it SHALL NOT list `ri-05` or any completed item.\n\n#### Scenario: Replan preserves completed items and learnings\nWHEN `/plan-roadmap --replan `replan-request.json` SHALL no longer exist\nAND `decomposer.py validate` SHALL exit 0.\n\n#### Scenario: Replan without a request file is refused\nWHEN `/plan-roadmap --replan <roadmap-id>` is invoked and `<workspace>/replan-request.json` does not exist\nTHEN the workflow SHALL exit with a structured error naming the missing file\nAND the roadmap SHALL be unchanged.\n\n### Requirement: Adaptive Roadmap Execution\n\nThe system SHALL provide an `autopilot-roadmap` workflow that executes roadmap items iteratively and updates pending items using implementation evidence. When an item fails, `CheckpointManager.fail_item(checkpoint, roadmap, item_id, reason, *, replan=False)` SHALL transition the failed item's dependents to `blocked` by default and to `replan_required` only when the failing item's outcome payload carries an explicit `replan: true` signal; the workflow SHALL NOT infer hard-versus-workaroundable from the failure text. For every item in `replan_required`, the orchestrator SHALL evaluate `Gate.REPLAN_REQUIRED` through an injected `GateEvaluator` (default `approval_gate.build_default_gate()`); on `proceed` it SHALL write a `ReplanRequest` conforming to `contracts/events/replan-request.schema.json` to `<workspace>/replan-request.json` and finish the run with status `replan_requested`; on `blocked` the items SHALL stay `replan_required`, the decision SHALL be recorded in the checkpoint, and the run SHALL continue with other ready items. The orchestrator SHALL make no LLM or network call to perform the replan itself; the host executes `/plan-roadmap --replan <roadmap-id>`.\n\n#### Scenario: Learning feedback updates remaining roadmap items\nWHEN a roadmap item completes implementation and review\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL persist a learning entry to `learnings/<item-id>.md` conforming to `contracts/learning-log.schema.json`\nAND it SHALL update the root `learning-log.md` index with a one-line summary\nAND before the next item begins it SHALL ingest prior learning entries (direct dependencies + most recent 3)\nAND it SHALL update pending item recommendations accordingly.\n\n#### Scenario: Resume from persisted checkpoint after interruption\nWHEN roadmap execution stops before completion\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL resume from the last successful checkpoint conforming to `contracts/checkpoint.schema.json`\nAND it SHALL skip phases already marked complete unless forced by user input.\n\n#### Scenario: Abort item execution when prerequisite roadmap dependency is incomplete\nWHEN a roadmap item is selected for execution\nAND one or more of its dependency items are not complete\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL block execution of that item\nAND it SHALL emit a dependency-blocked status with missing dependency IDs.\n\n#### Scenario: Handle individual roadmap item implementation failure\nWHEN a roadmap item fails implementation (tests fail, review rejects, or design dead-end)\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL mark the item as `failed` in `roadmap.yaml` with a structured failure reason\nAND it SHALL persist a learning entry recording the failure details, root cause, and recommendations\nAND it SHALL transition dependent items in `approved` or `candidate` status to `blocked`\nAND it SHALL proceed to the next eligible item rather than halting the entire roadmap.\n\n#### Scenario: Explicit replan signal produces replan_required\nWHEN a roadmap item fails and its outcome payload contains `replan: true`\nTHEN `fail_item(..., replan=True)` SHALL transition dependents in `approved` or `candidate` status to `replan_required` instead of `blocked`\nAND each such dependent SHALL record the failed item id in `blocked_by`\nAND the failed item itself SHALL still be marked `failed`.\n\n#### Scenario: Replan gate proceeds and emits a request\nWHEN at least one item is in `replan_required` after a failure is recorded\nAND `Gate.REPLAN_REQUIRED` evaluates to `proceed`\nTHEN the orchestrator SHALL write `<workspace>/replan-request.json` listing the `replan_required` item ids, the failed item id, and the gate decision\nAND the run summary status SHALL be `replan_requested`\nAND no item in `replan_required` SHALL be dispatched.\n\n#### Scenario: Replan gate blocked leaves items parked\nWHEN `Gate.REPLAN_REQUIRED` evaluates to `blocked` (posture `block`, timeout default block, or coordinator unreachable)\nTHEN no `replan-request.json` SHALL be written\nAND the affected items SHALL remain `replan_required`\nAND the decision SHALL be persisted in the checkpoint's `gate_decisions`\nAND the orchestrator SHALL continue with other ready items.\n\n#### Scenario: Orchestrator never performs the replan itself\nWHEN a replan request is emitted\nTHEN `skills/autopilot-roadmap/scripts/` SHALL contain no import of an LLM SDK and no network call to perform re-decomposition\nAND the host-assisted invariant test SHALL continue to pass.\n\n### Requirement: Usage-Limit-Aware Multi-Vendor Scheduling\n\nThe system SHALL apply explicit policy when vendor session/rate limits are encountered during roadmap execution.\n\n#### Scenario: Wait policy selected under budget constraints\nWHEN the preferred vendor hits a usage/session limit\nAND active policy is `wait_if_budget_exceeded`\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL pause execution until the known reset window\nAND it SHALL persist pause reason, blocked vendor, and expected resume `switch_if_time_saved`\nAND configured policy constraints allow alternate vendor cost\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL dispatch eligible work to an alternate vendor\nAND it SHALL persist expected and observed cost/latency deltas in `checkpoint.json`.\n\n#### Scenario: Cascading vendor failures with recursive policy evaluation\nWHEN the preferred vendor hits a usage/session limit\nAND the system progress does not depend on one model context window.\n\n#### Scenario: Progressive context reload per phase\nWHEN a roadmap phase starts\nTHEN the workflow SHALL load only required artifacts: roadmap artifact writers SHALL sanitize content before persisting to prevent secret exposure in durable, potentially committed state.\n\n#### Scenario: Redact sensitive content from learning entries\nWHEN writing a learning entry to `learnings/<item-id>.md`\nTHEN the writer SHALL pass the content through a sanitization utility\nAND the utility SHALL reject or redact: credentials, API keys, tokens, raw responses, authentication headers, or session tokens.\n\n### Requirement: Delegated Autopilot Item Lifecycle\n\nThe roadmap orchestrator SHALL provide an opt-in two-stage delegated lifecycle: prepare The child Autopilot run remains the sole writer of that change phase state.\n\n#### Scenario: Delegate one item lifecycle\n- **WHEN** a dependency-ready item with an exact `change_id` is executed in delegated-lifecycle mode\n- **THEN** prepare returns a durable batch ID and request without invoking `dispatch_fn`, and apply later invokes `dispatch_fn(item_id, \"autopilot\", context)` exactly once for that generation through the bound result lookup\n- **AND** the roadmap checkpoint is completed only after a successful structured dispatch result\n\n#### Scenario: Reject an item without an exact change identifier\n- **WHEN** delegated-lifecycle mode selects an item whose `change_id` is absent or invalid\n- **THEN** no background dispatch is admitted\n- **AND** the item and checkpoint remain invalid, empty, or boundless write-scope evidence\n- **THEN** the items are not admitted to the same batch and each affected request carries `proof: serial_indeterminate` with a schema-valid possibly **WHEN** two items declare globs whose intersection cannot be disproven, including `a/*/c` versus `a/b/*`\n- **THEN** the classifier returns `ambiguous` rather than `disjoint`\n- **AND** all package preserve unresolved attempts across session restart.\n\n#### Scenario: Persist a prepared batch before launch\n- **WHEN** the scheduler prepares a safe batch of delegated item requests\n- **THEN** each request's identity, exact isolation/scope/context envelope, stable launch token, marker path, attempt, phase, and prepared status are saved in `checkpoint.json` before the requests are emitted\n- **AND** a crash after preparation loses agent launch work rather than losing the identity of potentially running work\n\n#### Scenario: Resume with an unresolved attempt\n- **WHEN** a fresh supervisor loads a checkpoint containing a prepared attempt without a correlated result\n- **THEN** it reconciles a persisted host launch acknowledgement, an atomic child-start marker, and worktree Autopilot state before deciding whether work launched\n- **AND** pre-go stale claims may be reclaimed by generation compare-and-swap; after go, takeover requires positive task-death evidence, and unknown liveness becomes non-resumable quarantine\n\n#### Scenario: Reconcile lease crash windows\n- **WHEN** a crash occurs before marker creation, after marker but before Autopilot entry, before host acknowledgement, or while a child is active\n- **THEN** the generation-specific ack/go barrier prevents Autopilot entry before durable handle acknowledgement, while markers, heartbeats, handle status, exact worktree loop-state, and terminal handoff/result evidence classify the generation\n- **AND** a pre-go expired claim may be reclaimed safely, but a post-go generation may be reclaimed only after positive task-death evidence; mere absence or expiry enters quarantine\n- **AND** duplicate owners, active-lease token reuse, and stale owners that fail compare-and-swap are refused\n\n#### Scenario: Resume an authorized parked attempt\n- **WHEN** the supervise gate router supplies an `approval_ref` of the form `gate-decision:<decision_id>` for a `pending_gate` or `policy_pause` parked dispatch\n- **THEN** the resume command verifies the reference resolves to a `gate_decisions` record in the same checkpoint with outcome `proceed`, a gate equal to the parked gate (or `escalate_resume` for `policy_pause`), and a matching `dispatch_id`, then compare-and-swaps parked to prepared, increments the lease generation, and emits one continuation with the same dispatch ID, attempt, token, worktree, and loop-state\n- **AND** a reference that does not resolve, resolves to a `blocked` decision, or names a different gate or dispatch is rejected without mutating the attempt\n- **AND** the normal child-start protocol transitions it to launched while duplicate or unauthorized resumes are rejected\n- **AND** `ExecutionAdapter.prepare` likewise requires a `roadmap_approval_ref` resolving to a `proceed` `roadmap_approval` decision for the checkpoint's roadmap before any attempt is written\n\n#### Scenario: Quarantine unknown post-go liveness\n- **WHEN** a post-go generation has no duplicate Autopilot entry occurs\n- **AND** approval-gate resume is forbidden until reconciliation positively proves the prior task dead or terminal\n\n### Requirement: Roadmap items are refined before they are implemented\n\nAn item advanced to by the roadmap runtime SHALL enter the planning phase, so that its preliminary scaffold is refined using what was learned implementing its dependencies before any implementation begins.\n\nRoadmap items are planned one at a time rather than all at once precisely so that later items benefit from earlier ones. Advancing straight into implementation spends that opportunity and implements against a scaffold nobody revisited.\n\n#### Scenario: Advancing to the next item enters planning\nWHEN the roadmap runtime advances to the next ready item\nTHEN the checkpoint phase SHALL be set to planning\nAND the persisted checkpoint SHALL record that phase.\n\n#### Scenario: The refinement pass is not reported as already complete\nWHEN the roadmap runtime has just advanced to an item\nTHEN the planning phase SHALL NOT be reported as skippable for that item\nAND a refinement pass SHALL therefore run before implementation.\n\n#### Scenario: Refinement acts on the scaffold rather than an empty directory\nWHEN a refinement pass begins for a newly advanced item\nTHEN the item's change directory SHALL already contain the preliminary proposal and spec delta written at roadmap-creation time.\n\n### Requirement: Canonical Cross-Roadmap Readiness Resolution\n\nThe roadmap runtime SHALL expose a read-only repository-wide resolver that uses roadmap definitions plus canonical checkpoint state to emit one globally ranked ready-now list. The admission function `_get_ready_items` MUST have exactly one source definition in `roadmap-runtime` and SHALL be imported by both `autopilot-roadmap` and the repository-wide resolver.\n\n#### Scenario: Return one globally ranked ready-now list\n\n- **WHEN** the resolver scans multiple active roadmap workspaces containing dependency-ready items\n- **THEN** it SHALL return one flat list sorted by priority, roadmap id, and item id\n- **AND** each entry SHALL carry roadmap id, item id, priority, and effort.\n\n#### Scenario: Preserve the existing autopilot admission contract\n\n- **WHEN** autopilot asks for ready items in one roadmap\n- **THEN** the shared helper SHALL admit only approved or in-progress items whose local and external prerequisites are complete\n- **AND** it SHALL exclude checkpoint-completed, checkpoint-failed, superseded, and `superseded_by` items.\n\n#### Scenario: Use one shared implementation\n\n- **WHEN** the repository's Python sources are inspected by AST\n- **THEN** exactly one function definition named `_get_ready_items` SHALL exist under `skills/`\n- **AND** both the autopilot orchestrator and repository-wide resolver SHALL import that definition from `roadmap-runtime`.\n\n### Requirement: Checkpoint-Authoritative Cross-Roadmap Edges\n\nThe resolver SHALL treat a present valid checkpoint's completed and failed terminal sets as authoritative for its roadmap, and SHALL use roadmap item status only when the checkpoint is absent as a valid never-started state. Typed `external_depends_on` edges MUST remain blocked until their effective external prerequisite is completed.\n\n#### Scenario: External prerequisite completion unblocks without dependent edits\n\n- **GIVEN** supervisor item `ri-04` has `external_depends_on: [roadmap-always-on-agent-automation:ri-06]`\n- **WHEN** always-on `ri-06` is incomplete in its effective state\n- **THEN** supervisor Checkpoint terminal state overrides stale roadmap status\n\n- **WHEN** a valid checkpoint records an item completed or failed while its roadmap definition still says approved or in-progress\n- **THEN** the resolver SHALL exclude that item from ready output\n- **AND** external dependents SHALL observe completion only for the checkpoint-completed case.\n\n#### Scenario: Invalid checkpoint fails closed\n\n- **WHEN** a checkpoint is malformed, names a different roadmap, references unknown terminal item ids, or contradicts its own terminal sets\n- **THEN** the resolver SHALL mark that workspace stale with a bounded reason code\n- **AND** it SHALL withhold that workspace's items and completion refs instead of reconstructing state from advisory artifacts.\n#### Scenario: Valid checkpoint divergence remains authoritative\n\n- **WHEN** a structurally valid matching checkpoint has terminal sets that lag or lead terminal status fields in its roadmap\n- **THEN** the resolver SHALL emit a stale `roadmap_checkpoint_divergence` diagnostic without withholding the workspace\n- **AND** readiness and external completion SHALL continue to use the checkpoint terminal sets.\n\n#### Scenario: Invalid roadmap fails closed\n\n- **WHEN** an active roadmap is malformed or duplicates another active roadmap declared id\n- **THEN** the resolver SHALL emit `roadmap_invalid` or `duplicate_roadmap_id`, return non-zero from the CLI, and withhold affected workspace state.\n\n### Requirement: Deterministic Readiness Projection\n\nThe resolver SHALL derive its output only from active `roadmap.yaml` files and sibling `checkpoint.json` state. Its JSON output MUST contain a SHA-256 `source_fingerprint` over canonical readiness-relevant input, a content-consistency `stale` signal, and bounded diagnostics. A downstream projection can detect staleness by comparing its stored source fingerprint with a newly resolved fingerprint. It SHALL NOT contain a generated timestamp or depend on mtimes, learnings, handoffs, coordinator state, or queue projections.\n\n#### Scenario: Unchanged inputs produce byte-identical output\n\n- **WHEN** the readiness command runs twice with no roadmap or checkpoint content change\n- **THEN** the two stdout byte streams SHALL be identical\n- **AND** their source fingerprints SHALL be identical\n- **AND** ready entries, diagnostics, and keys SHALL use deterministic ordering.\n\n#### Scenario: Missing checkpoint is a valid first run\n\n- **WHEN** a valid roadmap workspace has no byte-identical\n- **THEN** the resolver output SHALL remain byte-identical.\n\n### Requirement: Approved candidate-work intake\n\n`/plan-roadmap` MUST provide a validated intake seam that maps one approved\ncandidate-work stub and operator-approved acceptance outcomes to one roadmap item\nwithout hand-editing intermediate artifacts.\n\n#### Scenario: Approved stub creates a new-roadmap effort, priority, and exact suggested change ID\n- **AND** the scaffolded spec delta SHALL use the approved capability\n- **AND** the item's description SHALL retain candidate provenance\n\n#### outcomes still scaffolds validly\nWHEN a scaffolded candidate declares no acceptance outcomes\nTHEN `plan-roadmap` SHALL still emit a delta that passes `openspec validate --strict`\nAND that delta sketch\nTHEN the artifact SHALL carry a marker identifying it as a scaffold awaiting refinement\nAND the marker SHALL name the roadmap and item it was generated from.\n\n#### Scenario: Design sketches neither\nTHEN no `design.md` SHALL be written.\n\n#### Scenario: Merge undersized roadmap items during decomposition\nWHEN decomposition produces candidate items that are smaller than a single implementable OpenSpec change\nTHEN `plan-roadmap` SHALL merge them with adjacent items\nAND it SHALL record the merge rationale in the merged item's description.\n\n#### Scenario: Split oversized dependents that are not in a preserved status)\nAND it SHALL NOT list `ri-05` or any completed item.\n\n#### Scenario: Replan preserves completed items and learnings\nWHEN `/plan-roadmap --replan `replan-request.json` SHALL no longer exist\nAND `decomposer.py validate` SHALL exit 0.\n\n#### Scenario: Replan without a request file is refused\nWHEN `/plan-roadmap --replan <roadmap-id>` is invoked and `<workspace>/replan-request.json` does not exist\nTHEN the workflow SHALL exit with a structured error naming the missing file\nAND the roadmap SHALL be unchanged.\n\n### Requirement: Adaptive Roadmap Execution\n\nThe system SHALL provide an `autopilot-roadmap` workflow that executes roadmap items iteratively and updates pending items using implementation evidence. When an item fails, `CheckpointManager.fail_item(checkpoint, roadmap, item_id, reason, *, replan=False)` SHALL transition the failed item's dependents to `blocked` by default and to `replan_required` only when the failing item's outcome payload carries an explicit `replan: true` signal; the workflow SHALL NOT infer hard-versus-workaroundable from the failure text. For every item in `replan_required`, the orchestrator SHALL evaluate `Gate.REPLAN_REQUIRED` through an injected `GateEvaluator` (default `approval_gate.build_default_gate()`); on `proceed` it SHALL write a `ReplanRequest` conforming to `contracts/events/replan-request.schema.json` to `<workspace>/replan-request.json` and finish the run with status `replan_requested`; on `blocked` the items SHALL stay `replan_required`, the decision SHALL be recorded in the checkpoint, and the run SHALL continue with other ready items. The orchestrator SHALL make no LLM or network call to perform the replan itself; the host executes `/plan-roadmap --replan <roadmap-id>`.\n\n#### Scenario: Learning feedback updates remaining roadmap items\nWHEN a roadmap item completes implementation and review\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL persist a learning entry to `learnings/<item-id>.md` conforming to `contracts/learning-log.schema.json`\nAND it SHALL update the root `learning-log.md` index with a one-line summary\nAND before the next item begins it SHALL ingest prior learning entries (direct dependencies + most recent 3)\nAND it SHALL update pending item recommendations accordingly.\n\n#### Scenario: Resume from persisted checkpoint after interruption\nWHEN roadmap execution stops before completion\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL resume from the last successful checkpoint conforming to `contracts/checkpoint.schema.json`\nAND it SHALL skip phases already marked complete unless forced by user input.\n\n#### Scenario: Abort item execution when prerequisite roadmap dependency is incomplete\nWHEN a roadmap item is selected for execution\nAND one or more of its dependency items are not complete\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL block execution of that item\nAND it SHALL emit a dependency-blocked status with missing dependency IDs.\n\n#### Scenario: Handle individual roadmap item implementation failure\nWHEN a roadmap item fails implementation (tests fail, review rejects, or design dead-end)\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL mark the item as `failed` in `roadmap.yaml` with a structured failure reason\nAND it SHALL persist a learning entry recording the failure details, root cause, and recommendations\nAND it SHALL transition dependent items in `approved` or `candidate` status to `blocked`\nAND it SHALL proceed to the next eligible item rather than halting the entire roadmap.\n\n#### Scenario: Explicit replan signal produces replan_required\nWHEN a roadmap item fails and its outcome payload contains `replan: true`\nTHEN `fail_item(..., replan=True)` SHALL transition dependents in `approved` or `candidate` status to `replan_required` instead of `blocked`\nAND each such dependent SHALL record the failed item id in `blocked_by`\nAND the failed item itself SHALL still be marked `failed`.\n\n#### Scenario: Replan gate proceeds and emits a request\nWHEN at least one item is in `replan_required` after a failure is recorded\nAND `Gate.REPLAN_REQUIRED` evaluates to `proceed`\nTHEN the orchestrator SHALL write `<workspace>/replan-request.json` listing the `replan_required` item ids, the failed item id, and the gate decision\nAND the run summary status SHALL be `replan_requested`\nAND no item in `replan_required` SHALL be dispatched.\n\n#### Scenario: Replan gate blocked leaves items parked\nWHEN `Gate.REPLAN_REQUIRED` evaluates to `blocked` (posture `block`, timeout default block, or coordinator unreachable)\nTHEN no `replan-request.json` SHALL be written\nAND the affected items SHALL remain `replan_required`\nAND the decision SHALL be persisted in the checkpoint's `gate_decisions`\nAND the orchestrator SHALL continue with other ready items.\n\n#### Scenario: Orchestrator never performs the replan itself\nWHEN a replan request is emitted\nTHEN `skills/autopilot-roadmap/scripts/` SHALL contain no import of an LLM SDK and no network call to perform re-decomposition\nAND the host-assisted invariant test SHALL continue to pass.\n\n### Requirement: Usage-Limit-Aware Multi-Vendor Scheduling\n\nThe system SHALL apply explicit policy when vendor session/rate limits are encountered during roadmap execution.\n\n#### Scenario: Wait policy selected under budget constraints\nWHEN the preferred vendor hits a usage/session limit\nAND active policy is `wait_if_budget_exceeded`\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL pause execution until the known reset window\nAND it SHALL persist pause reason, blocked vendor, and expected resume `switch_if_time_saved`\nAND configured policy constraints allow alternate vendor cost\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL dispatch eligible work to an alternate vendor\nAND it SHALL persist expected and observed cost/latency deltas in `checkpoint.json`.\n\n#### Scenario: Cascading vendor failures with recursive policy evaluation\nWHEN the preferred vendor hits a usage/session limit\nAND the system progress does not depend on one model context window.\n\n#### Scenario: Progressive context reload per phase\nWHEN a roadmap phase starts\nTHEN the workflow SHALL load only required artifacts: roadmap Observability\n\nRoadmap workflows SHALL emit structured log events to support debugging, auditing, and operational monitoring of long-running orchestration.\n\n#### Scenario: Structured logging for artifact writers SHALL sanitize content before persisting to prevent secret exposure in durable, potentially committed state.\n\n#### Scenario: Redact sensitive content from learning entries\nWHEN responses, authentication headers, or session tokens.\n\n### Requirement: Delegated Autopilot Item Lifecycle\n\nThe roadmap orchestrator SHALL provide an opt-in two-stage delegated lifecycle: prepare persists a batch without invoking `dispatch_fn`; apply invokes the existing synchronous callback exactly once per collected generation result with phase `autopilot`. The child Autopilot run remains the sole writer of that change phase state.\n\n#### Scenario: Delegate one item lifecycle\n- **WHEN** a dependency-ready item with an exact `change_id` is executed in delegated-lifecycle mode\n- **THEN** prepare returns a durable batch ID and request without invoking `dispatch_fn`, and apply later invokes `dispatch_fn(item_id, \"autopilot\", context)` exactly once for that generation through the bound result lookup\n- **AND** the roadmap checkpoint is completed only after a successful structured dispatch result\n\n#### Scenario: Reject an item without an exact change identifier\n- **WHEN** delegated-lifecycle mode selects an item whose `change_id` is absent or invalid\n- **THEN** no background dispatch is admitted\n- **AND** the item and checkpoint remain resumable with a deterministic failure reason\n\n### Requirement: Scope-Safe Ready Batches\n\nThe roadmap orchestrator MUST admit multiple items to the same ready batch only when their aggregated declared write scopes and lock keys prove that they are independent.\n\n#### Scenario: Fan out disjoint ready items\n- **WHEN** two dependency-ready items have valid work packages with disjoint `write_allow` scopes and lock keys\n- **THEN** both items are emitted in the same prepared host batch without invoking `dispatch_fn`\n- **AND** a synchronization-barrier test observes both host task handles live before either result is awaited\n\n#### Scenario: Serialize overlapping or indeterminate items\n- **WHEN** ready items overlap by write scope or lock key, or either item has missing, invalid, empty, or boundless write-scope evidence\n- **THEN** the items are not admitted to the same batch and each affected request carries `proof: serial_indeterminate` with a schema-valid possibly empty `write_allow`\n- **AND** deterministic priority and item-id ordering selects the first item while the remainder stay ready\n\n#### Scenario: Treat ambiguous glob intersection conservatively\n- **WHEN** two items declare globs whose intersection cannot be disproven, including `a/*/c` versus `a/b/*`\n- **THEN** the classifier returns `ambiguous` rather than `disjoint`\n- **AND** all package scopes, including integration and runtime-mirror write scopes, participate in the decision\n\n### Requirement: Outcome-Only Resume Contract\n\nThe roadmap orchestrator SHALL persist only structured a child returns a schema-valid success result correlated to the current dispatch identifier and change identifier\n- **THEN** the item is completed and its learning entry is written once only after preserve unresolved attempts across session restart.\n\n#### Scenario: Persist a prepared batch before launch\n- **WHEN** the scheduler prepares a safe batch of delegated item requests\n- **THEN** each request's identity, exact isolation/scope/context envelope, stable launch token, marker path, attempt, phase, and prepared status are saved in `checkpoint.json` before the requests are emitted\n- **AND** a crash after preparation loses agent launch work rather than losing the identity of potentially running work\n\n#### Scenario: Resume with an unresolved attempt\n- **WHEN** a fresh supervisor loads a checkpoint containing a prepared attempt without a correlated result\n- **THEN** it reconciles a persisted host launch acknowledgement, an atomic child-start marker, and worktree Autopilot state before deciding whether work launched\n- **AND** pre-go stale claims may be reclaimed by generation compare-and-swap; after go, takeover requires positive task-death evidence, and unknown liveness becomes non-resumable quarantine\n\n#### Scenario: Reconcile lease crash windows\n- **WHEN** a crash occurs before marker creation, after marker but before Autopilot entry, before host acknowledgement, or while a child is active\n- **THEN** the generation-specific ack/go barrier prevents Autopilot entry before durable handle acknowledgement, while markers, heartbeats, handle status, exact worktree loop-state, and terminal handoff/result evidence classify the generation\n- **AND** a pre-go expired claim may be reclaimed safely, but a post-go generation may be reclaimed only after positive task-death evidence; mere absence or expiry enters quarantine\n- **AND** duplicate owners, active-lease token reuse, and stale owners that fail compare-and-swap are refused\n\n#### Scenario: Resume an authorized parked attempt\n- **WHEN** the supervise gate router supplies an `approval_ref` of the form `gate-decision:<decision_id>` for a `pending_gate` or `policy_pause` parked dispatch\n- **THEN** the resume command verifies the reference resolves to a `gate_decisions` record in the same checkpoint with outcome `proceed`, a gate equal to the parked gate (or `escalate_resume` for `policy_pause`), and a matching `dispatch_id`, then compare-and-swaps parked to prepared, increments the lease generation, and emits one continuation with the same dispatch ID, attempt, token, worktree, and loop-state\n- **AND** a reference that does not resolve, resolves to a `blocked` decision, or names a different gate or dispatch is rejected without mutating the attempt\n- **AND** the normal child-start protocol transitions it to launched while duplicate or unauthorized resumes are rejected\n- **AND** `ExecutionAdapter.prepare` likewise requires a `roadmap_approval_ref` resolving to a `proceed` `roadmap_approval` decision for the checkpoint's roadmap before any attempt is written\n\n#### Scenario: Quarantine unknown post-go liveness\n- **WHEN** a post-go generation has no terminal result and its durable task handle cannot positively establish live or dead status\n- **THEN** the attempt becomes `quarantined` with its uncertain lease unreleased and no takeover or duplicate Autopilot entry occurs\n- **AND** approval-gate resume is forbidden until reconciliation positively proves the prior task dead or terminal\n\n### Requirement: Roadmap items are refined before they are implemented\n\nAn item advanced to by the roadmap runtime SHALL enter the planning phase, so that its preliminary scaffold is refined using what was learned implementing its dependencies before any implementation begins.\n\nRoadmap items are planned one at a time rather than all at once precisely so that later items benefit from earlier ones. Advancing straight into implementation spends that opportunity and implements against a scaffold nobody revisited.\n\n#### Scenario: Advancing to the next item enters planning\nWHEN the roadmap runtime advances to the next ready item\nTHEN the checkpoint phase SHALL be set to planning\nAND the persisted checkpoint SHALL record that phase.\n\n#### Scenario: The refinement pass is not reported as already complete\nWHEN the roadmap runtime has just advanced to an item\nTHEN the planning phase SHALL NOT be reported as skippable for that item\nAND a refinement pass SHALL therefore run before implementation.\n\n#### Scenario: Refinement acts on the scaffold rather than an empty directory\nWHEN a refinement pass begins for a newly advanced item\nTHEN the item's change directory SHALL already contain the preliminary proposal and spec delta written at roadmap-creation time.\n\n### Requirement: Canonical Cross-Roadmap Readiness Resolution\n\nThe roadmap runtime SHALL expose a read-only repository-wide resolver that uses roadmap definitions plus canonical checkpoint state to emit one globally ranked ready-now list. The admission function `_get_ready_items` MUST have exactly one source definition in `roadmap-runtime` and SHALL be imported by both `autopilot-roadmap` and the repository-wide resolver.\n\n#### Scenario: Return one globally ranked ready-now list\n\n- **WHEN** the resolver scans multiple active roadmap workspaces containing dependency-ready items\n- **THEN** it SHALL return one flat list sorted by priority, roadmap id, and item id\n- **AND** each entry SHALL carry roadmap id, item id, priority, and effort.\n\n#### Scenario: Preserve the existing autopilot admission contract\n\n- **WHEN** autopilot asks for ready items in one roadmap\n- **THEN** the shared helper SHALL admit only approved or in-progress items whose local and external prerequisites are complete\n- **AND** it SHALL exclude checkpoint-completed, checkpoint-failed, superseded, and `superseded_by` items.\n\n#### Scenario: Use one shared implementation\n\n- **WHEN** the repository's Python sources are inspected by AST\n- **THEN** exactly one function definition named `_get_ready_items` SHALL exist under `skills/`\n- **AND** both the autopilot orchestrator and repository-wide resolver SHALL import that definition from `roadmap-runtime`.\n\n### Requirement: Checkpoint-Authoritative Cross-Roadmap Edges\n\nThe resolver SHALL treat a present valid checkpoint's completed and failed terminal sets as authoritative for its roadmap, and SHALL use roadmap item status only when the checkpoint is absent as a valid never-started state. Typed `external_depends_on` edges MUST remain blocked until their effective external prerequisite is completed.\n\n#### Scenario: External prerequisite completion unblocks without dependent edits\n\n- **GIVEN** supervisor item `ri-04` has `external_depends_on: [roadmap-always-on-agent-automation:ri-06]`\n- **WHEN** always-on `ri-06` is incomplete in its effective state\n- **THEN** supervisor `ri-04` SHALL be absent from ready output\n- **AND** when the always-on checkpoint records `ri-06` completed, `ri-04` SHALL become ready without editing the supervisor roadmap.\n\n#### Scenario: Checkpoint terminal state overrides stale roadmap status\n\n- **WHEN** a valid checkpoint records an item completed or failed while its roadmap definition still says approved or in-progress\n- **THEN** the resolver SHALL exclude that item from ready output\n- **AND** external dependents SHALL observe completion only for the checkpoint-completed case.\n\n#### Scenario: Invalid checkpoint fails closed\n\n- **WHEN** a checkpoint is malformed, names a different roadmap, references unknown terminal item ids, or contradicts its own terminal sets\n- **THEN** the resolver SHALL mark that workspace stale with a bounded reason code\n- **AND** it SHALL withhold that workspace's items and completion refs instead of reconstructing state from advisory artifacts.\n#### Scenario: Valid checkpoint divergence remains authoritative\n\n- **WHEN** a structurally valid matching checkpoint has terminal sets that lag or lead terminal status fields in its roadmap\n- **THEN** the resolver SHALL emit a stale `roadmap_checkpoint_divergence` diagnostic without withholding the workspace\n- **AND** readiness and external completion SHALL continue to use the checkpoint terminal sets.\n\n#### Scenario: Invalid roadmap fails closed\n\n- **WHEN** an active roadmap is malformed or duplicates another active roadmap declared id\n- **THEN** the resolver SHALL emit `roadmap_invalid` or `duplicate_roadmap_id`, return non-zero from the CLI, and withhold affected workspace state.\n\n### Requirement: Deterministic Readiness Projection\n\nThe resolver SHALL derive its output only from active `roadmap.yaml` files and sibling `checkpoint.json` state. Its JSON output MUST contain a SHA-256 `source_fingerprint` over canonical readiness-relevant input, a content-consistency `stale` signal, and bounded diagnostics. A downstream projection can detect staleness by comparing its stored source fingerprint with a newly resolved fingerprint. It SHALL NOT contain a generated timestamp or depend on mtimes, learnings, handoffs, coordinator state, or queue projections.\n\n#### Scenario: Unchanged inputs produce byte-identical output\n\n- **WHEN** the readiness command runs twice with no roadmap or checkpoint content change\n- **THEN** the two stdout byte streams SHALL be identical\n- **AND** their source fingerprints SHALL be identical\n- **AND** ready entries, diagnostics, and keys SHALL use deterministic ordering.\n\n#### Scenario: Missing checkpoint is a valid first run\n\n- **WHEN** a valid roadmap workspace has no checkpoint and no advisory record claims prior progress\n- **THEN** the resolver SHALL evaluate roadmap definition status as the never-started baseline\n- **AND** it SHALL report `checkpoint_absent` without marking the report stale.\n\n#### Scenario: Advisory state cannot change readiness\n\n- **WHEN** learning, handoff, or queue artifacts change while every roadmap and checkpoint remains byte-identical\n- **THEN** the resolver output SHALL remain byte-identical.\n\n### Requirement: Approved candidate-work intake\n\n`/plan-roadmap` MUST provide a validated intake seam that maps one approved\ncandidate-work stub and operator-approved acceptance outcomes to one roadmap item\nwithout hand-editing intermediate artifacts.\n\n#### Scenario: Approved stub creates a new-roadmap
