Update Purpose after archive.\n## Requirements\n### Requirement: Proposal Decomposition into Roadmap Changes\n\nThe system SHALL provide a `plan-roadmap` workflow that decomposes a long-form markdown proposal into a prioritized set of OpenSpec change candidates, and SHALL scaffold each approved candidate as a change that already validates.\n\n#### Scenario: Decompose markdown proposal into roadmap candidates\nWHEN a user provides a long markdown proposal to `plan-roadmap`\nTHEN the workflow SHALL extract candidate capabilities, constraints, and phases\nAND it SHALL emit a roadmap artifact conforming to `contracts/roadmap.schema.json`\nAND each candidate SHALL include effort estimate and rationale.\n\n#### Scenario: Reject decomposition when proposal input is insufficient\nWHEN the input markdown omits required implementation intent (no actionable capabilities or constraints)\nTHEN `plan-roadmap` SHALL fail with a structured validation error\nAND it SHALL provide guidance for minimum required proposal sections.\n\n#### Scenario: Seed OpenSpec change scaffolds from approved candidates\nWHEN the user approves selected roadmap candidates\nTHEN `plan-roadmap` SHALL create draft OpenSpec change directories for each approved candidate\nAND each created change SHALL include a proposal scaffold with a `parent_roadmap` field linking back to the roadmap change-id and item-id.\n\n#### Scenario: Scaffolded changes are valid OpenSpec changes\nWHEN `plan-roadmap` scaffolds an approved candidate\nTHEN the created change SHALL include at least one spec delta file under `specs/<capability>/spec.md`\nAND that change SHALL pass `openspec validate --strict`\nAND the delta SHALL survive being committed, rather than relying on a directory that git does not track.\n\n#### Scenario: Spec deltas are derived from acceptance outcomes\nWHEN a scaffolded candidate declares acceptance outcomes\nTHEN each outcome SHALL become one requirement with at least one scenario\nAND each requirement's first body line SHALL contain SHALL or MUST\nAND an outcome that already states a modal verb SHALL NOT be wrapped in a second one.\n\n#### Scenario: A candidate without acceptance outcomes still scaffolds validly\nWHEN a scaffolded candidate declares no acceptance outcomes\nTHEN `plan-roadmap` SHALL still emit a delta that passes `openspec validate --strict`\nAND that delta SHALL state that its requirements are to be replaced during refinement.\n\n#### Scenario: Scaffolded artifacts declare themselves preliminary\nWHEN `plan-roadmap` writes a spec delta or design sketch\nTHEN the artifact SHALL carry a marker identifying it as a scaffold awaiting refinement\nAND the marker SHALL name the roadmap and item it was generated from.\n\n#### Scenario: Design sketches are written only when they carry content\nWHEN a scaffolded candidate declares a rationale or dependencies\nTHEN `plan-roadmap` SHALL write a `design.md` sketch for it\nAND WHEN the candidate declares neither\nTHEN no `design.md` SHALL be written.\n\n#### Scenario: Merge undersized roadmap items during decomposition\nWHEN decomposition produces candidate items that are smaller than a single implementable OpenSpec change\nTHEN `plan-roadmap` SHALL merge them with adjacent items\nAND it SHALL record the merge rationale in the merged item's description.\n\n#### Scenario: Split oversized roadmap items during decomposition\nWHEN a candidate item exceeds single-change scope (spans multiple independent capabilities or systems)\nTHEN `plan-roadmap` SHALL split it into separate items\nAND it SHALL add dependency edges between the resulting items where ordering matters.\n\n#### Scenario: Replan scope is the affected subgraph only\nWHEN `decomposer.py replan-scope <workspace>` runs against a roadmap where `ri-03` failed with a replan signal and `ri-04`, `ri-06` depend on it while `ri-05` is completed\nTHEN the output SHALL list exactly `ri-04` and `ri-06` (and their transitive dependents that are not in a preserved status)\nAND it SHALL NOT list `ri-05` or any completed item.\n\n#### Scenario: Replan preserves completed items and learnings\nWHEN `/plan-roadmap --replan <roadmap-id>` completes\nTHEN every item that was `completed`, `superseded`, or `in_progress` SHALL be byte-identical to its pre-replan entry\nAND every file under `learnings/` SHALL be unchanged\nAND `replan-request.json` SHALL no longer exist\nAND `decomposer.py validate` SHALL exit 0.\n\n#### Scenario: Replan without a request file is refused\nWHEN `/plan-roadmap --replan <roadmap-id>` is invoked and `<workspace>/replan-request.json` does not exist\nTHEN the workflow SHALL exit with a structured error naming the missing file\nAND the roadmap SHALL be unchanged.\n\n### Requirement: Adaptive Roadmap Execution\n\nThe system SHALL provide an `autopilot-roadmap` workflow that executes roadmap items iteratively and updates pending items using implementation evidence. When an item fails, `CheckpointManager.fail_item(checkpoint, roadmap, item_id, reason, *, replan=False)` SHALL transition the failed item's dependents to `blocked` by default and to `replan_required` only when the failing item's outcome payload carries an explicit `replan: true` signal; the workflow SHALL NOT infer hard-versus-workaroundable from the failure text. For every item in `replan_required`, the orchestrator SHALL evaluate `Gate.REPLAN_REQUIRED` through an injected `GateEvaluator` (default `approval_gate.build_default_gate()`); on `proceed` it SHALL write a `ReplanRequest` conforming to `contracts/events/replan-request.schema.json` to `<workspace>/replan-request.json` and finish the run with status `replan_requested`; on `blocked` the items SHALL stay `replan_required`, the decision SHALL be recorded in the checkpoint, and the run SHALL continue with other ready items. The orchestrator SHALL make no LLM or network call to perform the replan itself; the host executes `/plan-roadmap --replan <roadmap-id>`.\n\n#### Scenario: Learning feedback updates remaining roadmap items\nWHEN a roadmap item completes implementation and review\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL persist a learning entry to `learnings/<item-id>.md` conforming to `contracts/learning-log.schema.json`\nAND it SHALL update the root `learning-log.md` index with a one-line summary\nAND before the next item begins it SHALL ingest prior learning entries (direct dependencies + most recent 3)\nAND it SHALL update pending item recommendations accordingly.\n\n#### Scenario: Resume from persisted checkpoint after interruption\nWHEN roadmap execution stops before completion\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL resume from the last successful checkpoint conforming to `contracts/checkpoint.schema.json`\nAND it SHALL skip phases already marked complete unless forced by user input.\n\n#### Scenario: Abort item execution when prerequisite roadmap dependency is incomplete\nWHEN a roadmap item is selected for execution\nAND one or more of its dependency items are not complete\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL block execution of that item\nAND it SHALL emit a dependency-blocked status with missing dependency IDs.\n\n#### Scenario: Handle individual roadmap item implementation failure\nWHEN a roadmap item fails implementation (tests fail, review rejects, or design dead-end)\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL mark the item as `failed` in `roadmap.yaml` with a structured failure reason\nAND it SHALL persist a learning entry recording the failure details, root cause, and recommendations\nAND it SHALL transition dependent items in `approved` or `candidate` status to `blocked`\nAND it SHALL proceed to the next eligible item rather than halting the entire roadmap.\n\n#### Scenario: Explicit replan signal produces replan_required\nWHEN a roadmap item fails and its outcome payload contains `replan: true`\nTHEN `fail_item(..., replan=True)` SHALL transition dependents in `approved` or `candidate` status to `replan_required` instead of `blocked`\nAND each such dependent SHALL record the failed item id in `blocked_by`\nAND the failed item itself SHALL still be marked `failed`.\n\n#### Scenario: Replan gate proceeds and emits a request\nWHEN at least one item is in `replan_required` after a failure is recorded\nAND `Gate.REPLAN_REQUIRED` evaluates to `proceed`\nTHEN the orchestrator SHALL write `<workspace>/replan-request.json` listing the `replan_required` item ids, the failed item id, and the gate decision\nAND the run summary status SHALL be `replan_requested`\nAND no item in `replan_required` SHALL be dispatched.\n\n#### Scenario: Replan gate blocked leaves items parked\nWHEN `Gate.REPLAN_REQUIRED` evaluates to `blocked` (posture `block`, timeout default block, or coordinator unreachable)\nTHEN no `replan-request.json` SHALL be written\nAND the affected items SHALL remain `replan_required`\nAND the decision SHALL be persisted in the checkpoint's `gate_decisions`\nAND the orchestrator SHALL continue with other ready items.\n\n#### Scenario: Orchestrator never performs the replan itself\nWHEN a replan request is emitted\nTHEN `skills/autopilot-roadmap/scripts/` SHALL contain no import of an LLM SDK and no network call to perform re-decomposition\nAND the host-assisted invariant test SHALL continue to pass.\n\n### Requirement: Usage-Limit-Aware Multi-Vendor Scheduling\n\nThe system SHALL apply explicit policy when vendor session/rate limits are encountered during roadmap execution.\n\n#### Scenario: Wait policy selected under budget constraints\nWHEN the preferred vendor hits a usage/session limit\nAND active policy is `wait_if_budget_exceeded`\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL pause execution until the known reset window\nAND it SHALL persist pause reason, blocked vendor, and expected resume timestamp in `checkpoint.json`.\n\n#### Scenario: Switch policy selected when time saved exceeds configured threshold\nWHEN the preferred vendor hits a usage/session limit\nAND active policy is `switch_if_time_saved`\nAND configured policy constraints allow alternate vendor cost\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL dispatch eligible work to an alternate vendor\nAND it SHALL persist expected and observed cost/latency deltas in `checkpoint.json`.\n\n#### Scenario: Cascading vendor failures with recursive policy evaluation\nWHEN the preferred vendor hits a usage/session limit\nAND the system switches to an alternate vendor per policy\nAND the alternate vendor also fails or hits limits\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL apply the same policy evaluation recursively across remaining eligible vendors\nAND it SHALL track cumulative switch attempts against `max_switch_attempts_per_item` from `roadmap.yaml` policy\nAND when max attempts are exhausted it SHALL transition to fail-closed behavior.\n\n#### Scenario: Fail closed when no eligible vendor exists\nWHEN the preferred vendor is limited\nAND no alternate vendor satisfies capability and policy constraints (or max switch attempts exceeded)\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL transition the current item to `blocked` in `roadmap.yaml`\nAND it SHALL record required operator action to continue\nAND it SHALL persist the full vendor switch history in `checkpoint.json` for audit.\n\n### Requirement: Progressive Context Management\n\nRoadmap workflows SHALL externalize planning/execution context to durable artifacts so progress does not depend on one model context window.\n\n#### Scenario: Progressive context reload per phase\nWHEN a roadmap phase starts\nTHEN the workflow SHALL load only required artifacts: roadmap item, checkpoint, and relevant learning entries (direct dependencies + most recent 3)\nAND it SHALL avoid requiring full historical chat transcript\nAND total loaded learning entries SHALL NOT exceed the dependency fan-in plus a configurable recency window (default 3).\n\n#### Scenario: Learning log compaction for long roadmaps\nWHEN the root `learning-log.md` index exceeds 50 entries\nTHEN the workflow SHALL run a compaction pass that summarizes older entries into `learnings/_archive.md`\nAND it SHALL remove individual entry files no longer referenced by pending roadmap items\nAND compaction SHALL preserve all entries referenced by items with status `in_progress`, `blocked`, or `replan_required`.\n\n#### Scenario: Coordinator-backed context fallback\nWHEN coordinator context APIs are available\nTHEN the workflow SHALL publish phase summaries to coordinator memory\nAND when coordinator APIs are unavailable it SHALL continue using on-disk artifacts with equivalent content.\n\n#### Scenario: Artifact corruption detected during load\nWHEN a required roadmap artifact is malformed or missing required fields per its JSON Schema contract\nTHEN the workflow SHALL stop execution for that phase\nAND it SHALL report a recoverable artifact-validation error with repair instructions referencing the relevant schema file.\n\n### Requirement: Artifact Observability\n\nRoadmap workflows SHALL emit structured log events to support debugging, auditing, and operational monitoring of long-running orchestration.\n\n#### Scenario: Structured logging for item state transitions\nWHEN a roadmap item transitions between states (e.g., `approved` → `in_progress`, `in_progress` → `completed`)\nTHEN the workflow SHALL emit a structured log event containing: item_id, from_state, to_state, timestamp, and triggering_action.\n\n#### Scenario: Structured logging for policy decisions\nWHEN the policy engine evaluates a vendor limit event\nTHEN the workflow SHALL emit a structured log event containing: decision (wait/switch/fail-closed), vendor, reason, cost_delta (if applicable), and latency_delta (if applicable).\n\n#### Scenario: Structured logging for checkpoint operations\nWHEN a checkpoint is saved, restored, or advanced\nTHEN the workflow SHALL emit a structured log event containing: operation (save/restore/advance), item_id, phase, and timestamp.\n\n#### Scenario: Publish observability events to coordinator audit log\nWHEN coordinator audit APIs are available (`CAN_GUARDRAILS=true`)\nTHEN the workflow SHALL publish item transitions and policy decisions to the coordinator audit log\nAND when coordinator APIs are unavailable it SHALL continue with file-based logging only.\n\n### Requirement: Artifact Sanitization\n\nAll roadmap artifact writers SHALL sanitize content before persisting to prevent secret exposure in durable, potentially committed state.\n\n#### Scenario: Redact sensitive content from learning entries\nWHEN writing a learning entry to `learnings/<item-id>.md`\nTHEN the writer SHALL pass the content through a sanitization utility\nAND the utility SHALL reject or redact: credentials, API keys, tokens, raw vendor prompts/responses, environment variable values\nAND it SHALL preserve: structured summaries, decision rationale, cost/latency metrics, capability observations.\n\n#### Scenario: Validate sanitization on checkpoint writes\nWHEN writing `checkpoint.json`\nTHEN the writer SHALL ensure vendor_state and pause_state contain only structured metadata\nAND it SHALL NOT include raw error responses, authentication headers, or session tokens.\n\n### Requirement: Delegated Autopilot Item Lifecycle\n\nThe roadmap orchestrator SHALL provide an opt-in two-stage delegated lifecycle: prepare persists a batch without invoking `dispatch_fn`; apply invokes the existing synchronous callback exactly once per collected generation result with phase `autopilot`. The child Autopilot run remains the sole writer of that change phase state.\n\n#### Scenario: Delegate one item lifecycle\n- **WHEN** a dependency-ready item with an exact `change_id` is executed in delegated-lifecycle mode\n- **THEN** prepare returns a durable batch ID and request without invoking `dispatch_fn`, and apply later invokes `dispatch_fn(item_id, \"autopilot\", context)` exactly once for that generation through the bound result lookup\n- **AND** the roadmap checkpoint is completed only after a successful structured dispatch result\n\n#### Scenario: Reject an item without an exact change identifier\n- **WHEN** delegated-lifecycle mode selects an item whose `change_id` is absent or invalid\n- **THEN** no background dispatch is admitted\n- **AND** the item and checkpoint remain resumable with a deterministic failure reason\n\n### Requirement: Scope-Safe Ready Batches\n\nThe roadmap orchestrator MUST admit multiple items to the same ready batch only when their aggregated declared write scopes and lock keys prove that they are independent.\n\n#### Scenario: Fan out disjoint ready items\n- **WHEN** two dependency-ready items have valid work packages with disjoint `write_allow` scopes and lock keys\n- **THEN** both items are emitted in the same prepared host batch without invoking `dispatch_fn`\n- **AND** a synchronization-barrier test observes both host task handles live before either result is awaited\n\n#### Scenario: Serialize overlapping or indeterminate items\n- **WHEN** ready items overlap by write scope or lock key, or either item has missing, invalid, empty, or boundless write-scope evidence\n- **THEN** the items are not admitted to the same batch and each affected request carries `proof: serial_indeterminate` with a schema-valid possibly empty `write_allow`\n- **AND** deterministic priority and item-id ordering selects the first item while the remainder stay ready\n\n#### Scenario: Treat ambiguous glob intersection conservatively\n- **WHEN** two items declare globs whose intersection cannot be disproven, including `a/*/c` versus `a/b/*`\n- **THEN** the classifier returns `ambiguous` rather than `disjoint`\n- **AND** all package scopes, including integration and runtime-mirror write scopes, participate in the decision\n\n### Requirement: Outcome-Only Resume Contract\n\nThe roadmap orchestrator SHALL persist only structured dispatch outcomes and handoff identifiers needed to resume; it MUST NOT persist a child transcript in roadmap state or dispatch context.\n\n#### Scenario: Apply a successful child outcome\n- **WHEN** a child returns a schema-valid success result correlated to the current dispatch identifier and change identifier\n- **THEN** the item is completed and its learning entry is written once only after result path, branch, and loop-state evidence exactly match the prepared attempt and the resolved path remains contained by its verified worktree\n- **AND** contradictory status/outcome pairs are schema-invalid and the checkpoint records bounded outcome metadata without transcript content\n\n#### Scenario: Reject stale or mismatched child outcome\n- **WHEN** a result carries a different dispatch identifier, change identifier, or already-applied attempt\n- **THEN** the result is rejected without advancing the item\n- **AND** a resumed run can safely redispatch or reconcile the current attempt\n\n#### Scenario: Preserve a parked child\n- **WHEN** a child Autopilot run returns a schema-valid parked result for a pending gate or paused policy state\n- **THEN** the attempt is recorded as parked and the roadmap item is not marked failed or completed\n- **AND** dependents are not failure-blocked while the parked snapshot's bounded metadata (`kind`, `reason`, and the nullable `gate`, `deadline`, `resume_hint` the result contract permits — never an `approval_id`, which lives only in the supervise gate router's own ledger) remains available to that router, which is the only consumer permitted to resume it\n\n### Requirement: Durable Delegated Attempt Ledger\n\nThe roadmap checkpoint SHALL record every delegated dispatch attempt before its request is returned to the host and SHALL preserve unresolved attempts across session restart.\n\n#### Scenario: Persist a prepared batch before launch\n- **WHEN** the scheduler prepares a safe batch of delegated item requests\n- **THEN** each request's identity, exact isolation/scope/context envelope, stable launch token, marker path, attempt, phase, and prepared status are saved in `checkpoint.json` before the requests are emitted\n- **AND** a crash after preparation loses agent launch work rather than losing the identity of potentially running work\n\n#### Scenario: Resume with an unresolved attempt\n- **WHEN** a fresh supervisor loads a checkpoint containing a prepared attempt without a correlated result\n- **THEN** it reconciles a persisted host launch acknowledgement, an atomic child-start marker, and worktree Autopilot state before deciding whether work launched\n- **AND** pre-go stale claims may be reclaimed by generation compare-and-swap; after go, takeover requires positive task-death evidence, and unknown liveness becomes non-resumable quarantine\n\n#### Scenario: Reconcile lease crash windows\n- **WHEN** a crash occurs before marker creation, after marker but before Autopilot entry, before host acknowledgement, or while a child is active\n- **THEN** the generation-specific ack/go barrier prevents Autopilot entry before durable handle acknowledgement, while markers, heartbeats, handle status, exact worktree loop-state, and terminal handoff/result evidence classify the generation\n- **AND** a pre-go expired claim may be reclaimed safely, but a post-go generation may be reclaimed only after positive task-death evidence; mere absence or expiry enters quarantine\n- **AND** duplicate owners, active-lease token reuse, and stale owners that fail compare-and-swap are refused\n\n#### Scenario: Resume an authorized parked attempt\n- **WHEN** the supervise gate router supplies an `approval_ref` of the form `gate-decision:<decision_id>` for a `pending_gate` or `policy_pause` parked dispatch\n- **THEN** the resume command verifies the reference resolves to a `gate_decisions` record in the same checkpoint with outcome `proceed`, a gate equal to the parked gate (or `escalate_resume` for `policy_pause`), and a matching `dispatch_id`, then compare-and-swaps parked to prepared, increments the lease generation, and emits one continuation with the same dispatch ID, attempt, token, worktree, and loop-state\n- **AND** a reference that does not resolve, resolves to a `blocked` decision, or names a different gate or dispatch is rejected without mutating the attempt\n- **AND** the normal child-start protocol transitions it to launched while duplicate or unauthorized resumes are rejected\n- **AND** `ExecutionAdapter.prepare` likewise requires a `roadmap_approval_ref` resolving to a `proceed` `roadmap_approval` decision for the checkpoint's roadmap before any attempt is written\n\n#### Scenario: Quarantine unknown post-go liveness\n- **WHEN** a post-go generation has no terminal result and its durable task handle cannot positively establish live or dead status\n- **THEN** the attempt becomes `quarantined` with its uncertain lease unreleased and no takeover or duplicate Autopilot entry occurs\n- **AND** approval-gate resume is forbidden until reconciliation positively proves the prior task dead or terminal\n\n### Requirement: Roadmap items are refined before they are implemented\n\nAn item advanced to by the roadmap runtime SHALL enter the planning phase, so that its preliminary scaffold is refined using what was learned implementing its dependencies before any implementation begins.\n\nRoadmap items are planned one at a time rather than all at once precisely so that later items benefit from earlier ones. Advancing straight into implementation spends that opportunity and implements against a scaffold nobody revisited.\n\n#### Scenario: Advancing to the next item enters planning\nWHEN the roadmap runtime advances to the next ready item\nTHEN the checkpoint phase SHALL be set to planning\nAND the persisted checkpoint SHALL record that phase.\n\n#### Scenario: The refinement pass is not reported as already complete\nWHEN the roadmap runtime has just advanced to an item\nTHEN the planning phase SHALL NOT be reported as skippable for that item\nAND a refinement pass SHALL therefore run before implementation.\n\n#### Scenario: Refinement acts on the scaffold rather than an empty directory\nWHEN a refinement pass begins for a newly advanced item\nTHEN the item's change directory SHALL already contain the preliminary proposal and spec delta written at roadmap-creation time.\n\n### Requirement: Canonical Cross-Roadmap Readiness Resolution\n\nThe roadmap runtime SHALL expose a read-only repository-wide resolver that uses roadmap definitions plus canonical checkpoint state to emit one globally ranked ready-now list. The admission function `_get_ready_items` MUST have exactly one source definition in `roadmap-runtime` and SHALL be imported by both `autopilot-roadmap` and the repository-wide resolver.\n\n#### Scenario: Return one globally ranked ready-now list\n\n- **WHEN** the resolver scans multiple active roadmap workspaces containing dependency-ready items\n- **THEN** it SHALL return one flat list sorted by priority, roadmap id, and item id\n- **AND** each entry SHALL carry roadmap id, item id, priority, and effort.\n\n#### Scenario: Preserve the existing autopilot admission contract\n\n- **WHEN** autopilot asks for ready items in one roadmap\n- **THEN** the shared helper SHALL admit only approved or in-progress items whose local and external prerequisites are complete\n- **AND** it SHALL exclude checkpoint-completed, checkpoint-failed, superseded, and `superseded_by` items.\n\n#### Scenario: Use one shared implementation\n\n- **WHEN** the repository's Python sources are inspected by AST\n- **THEN** exactly one function definition named `_get_ready_items` SHALL exist under `skills/`\n- **AND** both the autopilot orchestrator and repository-wide resolver SHALL import that definition from `roadmap-runtime`.\n\n### Requirement: Checkpoint-Authoritative Cross-Roadmap Edges\n\nThe resolver SHALL treat a present valid checkpoint's completed and failed terminal sets as authoritative for its roadmap, and SHALL use roadmap item status only when the checkpoint is absent as a valid never-started state. Typed `external_depends_on` edges MUST remain blocked until their effective external prerequisite is completed.\n\n#### Scenario: External prerequisite completion unblocks without dependent edits\n\n- **GIVEN** supervisor item `ri-04` has `external_depends_on: [roadmap-always-on-agent-automation:ri-06]`\n- **WHEN** always-on `ri-06` is incomplete in its effective state\n- **THEN** supervisor `ri-04` SHALL be absent from ready output\n- **AND** when the always-on checkpoint records `ri-06` completed, `ri-04` SHALL become ready without editing the supervisor roadmap.\n\n#### Scenario: Checkpoint terminal state overrides stale roadmap status\n\n- **WHEN** a valid checkpoint records an item completed or failed while its roadmap definition still says approved or in-progress\n- **THEN** the resolver SHALL exclude that item from ready output\n- **AND** external dependents SHALL observe completion only for the checkpoint-completed case.\n\n#### Scenario: Invalid checkpoint fails closed\n\n- **WHEN** a checkpoint is malformed, names a different roadmap, references unknown terminal item ids, or contradicts its own terminal sets\n- **THEN** the resolver SHALL mark that workspace stale with a bounded reason code\n- **AND** it SHALL withhold that workspace's items and completion refs instead of reconstructing state from advisory artifacts.\n#### Scenario: Valid checkpoint divergence remains authoritative\n\n- **WHEN** a structurally valid matching checkpoint has terminal sets that lag or lead terminal status fields in its roadmap\n- **THEN** the resolver SHALL emit a stale `roadmap_checkpoint_divergence` diagnostic without withholding the workspace\n- **AND** readiness and external completion SHALL continue to use the checkpoint terminal sets.\n\n#### Scenario: Invalid roadmap fails closed\n\n- **WHEN** an active roadmap is malformed or duplicates another active roadmap declared id\n- **THEN** the resolver SHALL emit `roadmap_invalid` or `duplicate_roadmap_id`, return non-zero from the CLI, and withhold affected workspace state.\n\n### Requirement: Deterministic Readiness Projection\n\nThe resolver SHALL derive its output only from active `roadmap.yaml` files and sibling `checkpoint.json` state. Its JSON output MUST contain a SHA-256 `source_fingerprint` over canonical readiness-relevant input, a content-consistency `stale` signal, and bounded diagnostics. A downstream projection can detect staleness by comparing its stored source fingerprint with a newly resolved fingerprint. It SHALL NOT contain a generated timestamp or depend on mtimes, learnings, handoffs, coordinator state, or queue projections.\n\n#### Scenario: Unchanged inputs produce byte-identical output\n\n- **WHEN** the readiness command runs twice with no roadmap or checkpoint content change\n- **THEN** the two stdout byte streams SHALL be identical\n- **AND** their source fingerprints SHALL be identical\n- **AND** ready entries, diagnostics, and keys SHALL use deterministic ordering.\n\n#### Scenario: Missing checkpoint is a valid first run\n\n- **WHEN** a valid roadmap workspace has no checkpoint and no advisory record claims prior progress\n- **THEN** the resolver SHALL evaluate roadmap definition status as the never-started baseline\n- **AND** it SHALL report `checkpoint_absent` without marking the report stale.\n\n#### Scenario: Advisory state cannot change readiness\n\n- **WHEN** learning, handoff, or queue artifacts change while every roadmap and checkpoint remains byte-identical\n- **THEN** the resolver output SHALL remain byte-identical.\n\n### Requirement: Approved candidate-work intake\n\n`/plan-roadmap` MUST provide a validated intake seam that maps one approved\ncandidate-work stub and operator-approved acceptance outcomes to one roadmap item\nwithout hand-editing intermediate artifacts.\n\n#### Scenario: Approved stub creates a new-roadmap item\n\n- **WHEN** an approved canonical stub targets a new roadmap and supplies measurable acceptance outcomes, a roadmap ID, and a capability\n- **THEN** plan-roadmap SHALL create a schema-valid roadmap item\n- **AND** it SHALL create a complete schema-version-1 roadmap envelope using `provenance.source_artifact` as `source_proposal`\n- **AND** the item SHALL preserve title, rationale, effort, priority, and exact suggested change ID\n- **AND** the scaffolded spec delta SHALL use the approved capability\n- **AND** the item's description SHALL retain candidate provenance\n\n#### Scenario: Approved stub targets an existing roadmap\n\n- **WHEN** an approved canonical stub targets an existing roadmap workspace\n- **THEN** plan-roadmap SHALL route the mapped item through a refine-roadmap add request\n- **AND** the request SHALL omit execution priority so refine-roadmap assigns the next free priority\n- **AND** the candidate priority SHALL remain present in the request rationale\n- **AND** the existing roadmap SHALL NOT be written before preview and apply authorization\n\n#### Scenario: Approved stub omits acceptance outcomes\n\n- **WHEN** candidate intake is requested without non-empty acceptance outcomes\n- **THEN** plan-roadmap MUST refuse the request\n- **AND** no roadmap or change scaffold SHALL be written\n\n#### Scenario: Candidate dependencies retain explicit resolution\n\n- **WHEN** the shared resolver groups exact dependency matches across candidate, roadmap, active-change, and archive sources\n- **THEN** plan-roadmap SHALL collapse duplicate completed/archive lifecycle records and record an all-completed group as satisfied rationale\n- **AND** exactly one live target-roadmap item SHALL map to its local item ID and exactly one live item in another roadmap SHALL map to the canonical external reference\n- **AND** the preview SHALL show that conversion without silently dropping the source change ID\n\n#### Scenario: Candidate dependency cannot be resolved\n\n- **WHEN** a stub dependency is unknown, has multiple live matches, points to active work without a unique roadmap item, or has only failed/skipped/superseded records\n- **THEN** plan-roadmap MUST fail with the unresolved dependency name\n- **AND** it MUST NOT silently drop or rewrite the dependency\n\n#### Scenario: Approved input is a batch or collides with existing work\n\n- **WHEN** intake receives an array, a change ID already present in any roadmap item or active/archive change, or an ambiguous dependency\n- **THEN** plan-roadmap MUST refuse before roadmap or scaffold writes\n- **AND** the error SHALL identify the collision\n\n#### Scenario: Existing-roadmap request is previewable\n\n- **WHEN** one approved stub and nonblank outcomes target an existing roadmap\n- **THEN** plan-roadmap SHALL freshly load the workspace and place exactly one add operation with the next free item ID into the request immediately before preview\n- Bundled configuration SHALL declare location and identity\nmapping explicitly; implementations SHALL NOT infer them from lane names, commands, or catalog\npublishers.\n\n#### Scenario: List configured lanes\n\nWHEN an authorized client requests `GET /vendors`\nTHEN every configured lane SHALL include identity fields, location, capabilities, archetypes,\nisolation, transport, dispatch modes, dispatchability, effective availability, and catalog price\nprojections.\n\n#### Scenario: Dispatchability is configuration, not health\n\nWHEN a lane has an executable configured transport or adapter\nTHEN `dispatchable` SHALL be true independently of live availability\nAND automatic candidates SHALL require both dispatchability and eligible availability.\n\n#### Scenario: Filter eligible lanes\n\nWHEN a client supplies capability, archetype, dispatch-mode, location, or available-only filters\nTHEN every returned lane SHALL satisfy all supplied filters.\n\n#### Scenario: Lane-specific state\n\nWHEN one of two lanes for the same vendor type is unavailable\nTHEN their availability SHALL remain independent\nAND provider-level consumers MAY group them by `vendor_type`.\n\n#### Scenario: Unknown or ambiguous identity\n\nWHEN a request names an unknown lane or a provider-only identity matching multiple lanes\nTHEN the coordinator SHALL reject it without creating or fanning out state.\n\n### Requirement: Catalog-Owned Cost and Local Health\n\nThe registry SHALL batch-project price and local health from dg-00 `model_catalog` using explicit\nconfigured join fields and SHALL NOT persist a second price table.\n\n#### Scenario: Exact catalog projection\n\nWHEN a lane has models authored in its CLI/SDK config or existing provider model map\nTHEN exact model ID SHALL be the primary catalog join, endpoint kind/base URL SHALL constrain it\nwhen configured, optional catalog vendor SHALL further constrain it, and returned rows SHALL include\nmodel, endpoint, prompt/completion price, availability, refreshed time, and stale provenance.\n\n#### Scenario: Missing or ambiguous catalog row\n\nWHEN no unique configured join can identify a catalog row\nTHEN the cost projection and request quote SHALL be unknown\nAND the miss SHALL be audited without heuristic matching.\n\n#### Scenario: Local catalog gate\n\nWHEN a lane with `endpoint_kind=local` has no non-stale available matching catalog model\nTHEN it SHALL NOT be reported available even if its readiness probe succeeds\nAND location-local cloud CLI lanes SHALL NOT be subjected to this gate.\n\n#### Scenario: Request-scoped quote\n\nWHEN policy supplies an exact model plus estimated prompt and completion token counts\nTHEN the registry price projection SHALL produce the decimal USD quote defined in D8\nAND static tiers SHALL NOT populate USD deltas or enforce USD ceilings.\n\n### Requirement: Fresh Probe Availability\n\nThe existing watchdog SHALL persist every lane probe snapshot, including the first baseline, with\n`stale_after = observed_at + 2 × VENDOR_HEALTH_INTERVAL_SECONDS`.\n\n#### Scenario: First watchdog poll\n\nWHEN the watchdog completes its first vendor-health poll\nTHEN it SHALL persist each snapshot without emitting transition events.\n\n#### Scenario: Later transition\n\nWHEN a later poll changes health\nTHEN it SHALL refresh the snapshot and preserve existing `vendor.unavailable` or\n`vendor.recovered` events.\n\n#### Scenario: Probe becomes stale\n\nWHEN current time is at or after `stale_after`\nTHEN the probe SHALL contribute `unknown`, not its old status.\n\n#### Scenario: Lane has no probe method\n\nWHEN a configured lane has no CLI or other readiness probe\nTHEN watchdog SHALL persist `unknown` with reason `no_probe_method` rather than omit it.\n\n#### Scenario: Snapshot write fails\n\nWHEN one lane snapshot cannot be persisted\nTHEN the failure SHALL be audited and logged\nAND other snapshots and legacy transition events SHALL still be processed.\n\n#### Scenario: Deployed probe\n\nWHEN the coordinator watchdog runs in its production image\nTHEN it SHALL resolve the probe through `SKILLS_ROOT`, load the explicit `AGENTS_YAML` roster,\nstart independently of notification channels, and persist at least one configured snapshot.\n\n### Requirement: Bounded Rate-Limit State\n\nAuthenticated dispatchers SHALL report lane-scoped rate limits with an idempotency key. Every\naccepted limit SHALL have a server-normalized, non-null reset time bounded by configuration.\n\n#### Scenario: Absolute or relative reset\n\nWHEN exactly one of future `reset_at` or bounded `retry_after_seconds` is supplied\nTHEN the server SHALL normalize it to an absolute reset using server receipt time for retry-after.\n\n#### Scenario: Reset is omitted\n\nWHEN neither reset field is supplied\nTHEN the server SHALL apply `VENDOR_UNKNOWN_LIMIT_TTL_SECONDS` (default 900).\n\n#### Scenario: Conflicting reset fields\n\nWHEN both reset fields are supplied or a reset exceeds the configured maximum\nTHEN the coordinator SHALL reject the request.\n\n#### Scenario: Replay and conflict\n\nWHEN an observation ID is replayed with identical normalized content\nTHEN it SHALL be idempotent\nBUT a replay with different content SHALL return conflict.\n\n#### Scenario: Limit expires\n\nWHEN current time is at or after reset\nTHEN the limit SHALL stop affecting availability, SHALL be omitted from active reads, and SHALL\nbe retained only for the bounded audit-retention period.\n\n### Requirement: Authorized and Observable Ingestion\n\nThe coordinator SHALL bind observation identity to the authenticated principal, derive source and\nreceipt time server-side, and require either the explicit `report_vendor_rate_limit` operation or\na trust-level 3 administrative override for cross-lane writes.\n\n#### Scenario: Principal reports own lane\n\nWHEN a principal reports its own lane and the payload is valid\nTHEN the coordinator SHALL accept it and emit a structured audit record.\n\n#### Scenario: Principal targets another lane\n\nWHEN a dispatcher principal with `report_vendor_rate_limit` targets the concrete lane it dispatched\nTHEN the coordinator SHALL authorize the write even when source and target lanes differ.\n\n#### Scenario: Principal lacks reporting authority\n\nWHEN a non-administrator without the reporting operation targets another lane\nTHEN the coordinator SHALL return forbidden and SHALL NOT change state.\n\n#### Scenario: Observation lifecycle telemetry\n\nWHEN an observation is accepted, duplicated, rejected, expired, or compacted\nTHEN a structured audit/log record SHALL identify the lane, outcome, and non-secret reason.\n\n### Requirement: Repository-Native Registry Bridge\n\nThe coordination bridge SHALL expose normalized list, availability-detail, and rate-limit write\nhelpers using existing authentication headers and existing status/operation/response-or-error\nconventions.\n\n#### Scenario: Coordinator is unavailable\n\nWHEN a bridge operation encounters timeout, auth failure, not-found, server error, or malformed\npayload\nTHEN it SHALL preserve that distinct error and SHALL NOT return an empty successful registry.\n\n#### Scenario: Reporting fails after dispatch\n\nWHEN a rate-limit report cannot be persisted\nTHEN the original dispatch result SHALL remain unchanged\nAND the reporting failure SHALL be observable.\n\n### Requirement: Exact Dispatcher Attribution\n\nDispatch result collectors SHALL report rate limits using the selected concrete `agent_id` and\navailable reset metadata.\n\n#### Scenario: Adapter has lane context\n\nWHEN a dispatcher classifies a terminal capacity failure\nTHEN its additive result carrier SHALL report the exact selected lane through the bridge once.\n\n#### Scenario: One model limits before fallback succeeds\n\nWHEN an adapter observes a model capacity failure and later succeeds on another model\nTHEN its per-attempt callback SHALL report the failed model as a model-scoped limit\nAND the successful lane SHALL remain available for the fallback model.\n\n#### Scenario: Legacy policy signal lacks lane\n\nWHEN a legacy `vendor_limit:<policy_vendor>:<reason>` outcome has no\n`dispatch_agent_id` in context\nTHEN the orchestrator SHALL skip durable persistence as ambiguous\nAND SHALL exclude all lanes with that policy vendor for the current in-run decision only\nAND SHALL record the skip and provider-scope exclusion in structured decision provenance.\n\n### Requirement: Registry-Driven Roadmap Policy\n\nThe roadmap orchestrator SHALL obtain eligible lanes from a registry provider rather than a\nhardcoded roster and SHALL preserve lane identity through selection and decision provenance.\n\n#### Scenario: Registry is available\n\nWHEN a roadmap dispatch is limited with a concrete lane\nTHEN candidates SHALL satisfy required capability, phase archetype, dispatch mode, location, model\nlimit, and effective availability\nAND only the concrete limited lane SHALL be excluded before provider grouping.\n\n#### Scenario: Registry is unavailable\n\nWHEN the registry read fails\nTHEN automatic switching SHALL fail closed by default\nUNLESS an explicit policy permits an injected agents.yaml-derived provider with unknown\navailability\nAND no fallback SHALL embed availability, prices, or a vendor roster.\n\n#### Scenario: Cost ceiling has no exact quote\n\nWHEN policy configures a USD ceiling but structured model/token estimates or catalog price are absent\nTHEN static tiers SHALL NOT enforce the ceiling\nAND the decision SHALL record `cost_guard=unavailable` and continue under availability policy.\n\n#### Scenario: Model-scoped limit has an alternate model\n\nWHEN one model is limited but the same lane has another eligible model\nTHEN the lane SHALL remain available for the alternate model.\n"}]},"isError":false}

roadmap-orchestration Specification\n\n## Purpose\nTBD - created by archiving change roadmap-openspec-orchestration. Update Purpose after archive.\n## Requirements\n### Requirement: Proposal Decomposition into Roadmap Changes\n\nThe system SHALL provide a `plan-roadmap` workflow that decomposes a long-form markdown proposal into a prioritized set of OpenSpec change candidates, and SHALL scaffold each approved candidate as a change that already validates.\n\n#### Scenario: Decompose markdown proposal into roadmap candidates\nWHEN a user provides a long markdown proposal to `plan-roadmap`\nTHEN the workflow SHALL extract candidate capabilities, constraints, and phases\nAND it SHALL emit a roadmap artifact conforming to `contracts/roadmap.schema.json`\nAND each candidate SHALL include effort estimate and rationale.\n\n#### Scenario: Reject decomposition when proposal input is insufficient\nWHEN the input markdown omits required implementation intent (no actionable capabilities or constraints)\nTHEN `plan-roadmap` SHALL fail with a structured validation error\nAND it SHALL provide guidance for minimum required proposal sections.\n\n#### Scenario: Seed OpenSpec change scaffolds from approved candidates\nWHEN the user approves selected roadmap candidates\nTHEN `plan-roadmap` SHALL create draft OpenSpec change directories for each approved candidate\nAND each created change SHALL include a proposal scaffold with a `parent_roadmap` field linking back to the roadmap change-id and item-id.\n\n#### Scenario: Scaffolded changes are valid OpenSpec changes\nWHEN `plan-roadmap` scaffolds an approved candidate\nTHEN the created change SHALL include at least one spec delta file under `specs/<capability>/spec.md`\nAND that change SHALL pass `openspec validate --strict`\nAND the delta SHALL survive being committed, rather than relying on a directory that git does not track.\n\n#### Scenario: Spec deltas are derived from acceptance outcomes\nWHEN a scaffolded candidate declares acceptance outcomes\nTHEN each outcome SHALL become one requirement with at least one scenario\nAND each requirement's first body line SHALL contain SHALL or MUST\nAND an outcome that already states a modal verb SHALL NOT be wrapped in a second one.\n\n#### Scenario: A candidate without acceptance outcomes still scaffolds validly\nWHEN a scaffolded candidate declares no acceptance outcomes\nTHEN `plan-roadmap` SHALL still emit a delta that passes `openspec validate --strict`\nAND that delta SHALL state that its requirements are to be replaced during refinement.\n\n#### Scenario: Scaffolded artifacts declare themselves preliminary\nWHEN `plan-roadmap` writes a spec delta or design sketch\nTHEN the artifact SHALL carry a marker identifying it as a scaffold awaiting refinement\nAND the marker SHALL name the roadmap and item it was generated from.\n\n#### Scenario: Design sketches are written only when they carry content\nWHEN a scaffolded candidate declares a rationale or dependencies\nTHEN `plan-roadmap` SHALL write a `design.md` sketch for it\nAND WHEN the candidate declares neither\nTHEN no `design.md` SHALL be written.\n\n#### Scenario: Merge undersized roadmap items during decomposition\nWHEN decomposition produces candidate items that are smaller than a single implementable OpenSpec change\nTHEN `plan-roadmap` SHALL merge them with adjacent items\nAND it SHALL record the merge rationale in the merged item's description.\n\n#### Scenario: Split oversized roadmap items during decomposition\nWHEN a candidate item exceeds single-change scope (spans multiple independent capabilities or systems)\nTHEN `plan-roadmap` SHALL split it into separate items\nAND it SHALL add dependency edges between the resulting items where ordering matters.\n\n#### Scenario: Replan scope is the affected subgraph only\nWHEN `decomposer.py replan-scope <workspace>` runs against a roadmap where `ri-03` failed with a replan signal and `ri-04`, `ri-06` depend on it while `ri-05` is completed\nTHEN the output SHALL list exactly `ri-04` and `ri-06` (and their transitive dependents that are not in a preserved status)\nAND it SHALL NOT list `ri-05` or any completed item.\n\n#### Scenario: Replan preserves completed items and learnings\nWHEN `/plan-roadmap --replan <roadmap-id>` completes\nTHEN every item that was `completed`, `superseded`, or `in_progress` SHALL be byte-identical to its pre-replan entry\nAND every file under `learnings/` SHALL be unchanged\nAND `replan-request.json` SHALL no longer exist\nAND `decomposer.py validate` SHALL exit 0.\n\n#### Scenario: Replan without a request file is refused\nWHEN `/plan-roadmap --replan <roadmap-id>` is invoked and `<workspace>/replan-request.json` does not exist\nTHEN the workflow SHALL exit with a structured error naming the missing file\nAND the roadmap SHALL be unchanged.\n\n### Requirement: Adaptive Roadmap Execution\n\nThe system SHALL provide an `autopilot-roadmap` workflow that executes roadmap items iteratively and updates pending items using implementation evidence. When an item fails, `CheckpointManager.fail_item(checkpoint, roadmap, item_id, reason, *, replan=False)` SHALL transition the failed item's dependents to `blocked` by default and to `replan_required` only when the failing item's outcome payload carries an explicit `replan: true` signal; the workflow SHALL NOT infer hard-versus-workaroundable from the failure text. For every item in `replan_required`, the orchestrator SHALL evaluate `Gate.REPLAN_REQUIRED` through an injected `GateEvaluator` (default `approval_gate.build_default_gate()`); on `proceed` it SHALL write a `ReplanRequest` conforming to `contracts/events/replan-request.schema.json` to `<workspace>/replan-request.json` and finish the run with status `replan_requested`; on `blocked` the items SHALL stay `replan_required`, the decision SHALL be recorded in the checkpoint, and the run SHALL continue with other ready items. The orchestrator SHALL make no LLM or network call to perform the replan itself; the host executes `/plan-roadmap --replan <roadmap-id>`.\n\n#### Scenario: Learning feedback updates remaining roadmap items\nWHEN a roadmap item completes implementation and review\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL persist a learning entry to `learnings/<item-id>.md` conforming to `contracts/learning-log.schema.json`\nAND it SHALL update the root `learning-log.md` index with a one-line summary\nAND before the next item begins it SHALL ingest prior learning entries (direct dependencies + most recent 3)\nAND it SHALL update pending item recommendations accordingly.\n\n#### Scenario: Resume from persisted checkpoint after interruption\nWHEN roadmap execution stops before completion\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL resume from the last successful checkpoint conforming to `contracts/checkpoint.schema.json`\nAND it SHALL skip phases already marked complete unless forced by user input.\n\n#### Scenario: Abort item execution when prerequisite roadmap dependency is incomplete\nWHEN a roadmap item is selected for execution\nAND one or more of its dependency items are not complete\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL block execution of that item\nAND it SHALL emit a dependency-blocked status with missing dependency IDs.\n\n#### Scenario: Handle individual roadmap item implementation failure\nWHEN a roadmap item fails implementation (tests fail, review rejects, or design dead-end)\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL mark the item as `failed` in `roadmap.yaml` with a structured failure reason\nAND it SHALL persist a learning entry recording the failure details, root cause, and recommendations\nAND it SHALL transition dependent items in `approved` or `candidate` status to `blocked`\nAND it SHALL proceed to the next eligible item rather than halting the entire roadmap.\n\n#### Scenario: Explicit replan signal produces replan_required\nWHEN a roadmap item fails and its outcome payload contains `replan: true`\nTHEN `fail_item(..., replan=True)` SHALL transition dependents in `approved` or `candidate` status to `replan_required` instead of `blocked`\nAND each such dependent SHALL record the failed item id in `blocked_by`\nAND the failed item itself SHALL still be marked `failed`.\n\n#### Scenario: Replan gate proceeds and emits a request\nWHEN at least one item is in `replan_required` after a failure is recorded\nAND `Gate.REPLAN_REQUIRED` evaluates to `proceed`\nTHEN the orchestrator SHALL write `<workspace>/replan-request.json` listing the `replan_required` item ids, the failed item id, and the gate decision\nAND the run summary status SHALL be `replan_requested`\nAND no item in `replan_required` SHALL be dispatched.\n\n#### Scenario: Replan gate blocked leaves items parked\nWHEN `Gate.REPLAN_REQUIRED` evaluates to `blocked` (posture `block`, timeout default block, or coordinator unreachable)\nTHEN no `replan-request.json` SHALL be written\nAND the affected items SHALL remain `replan_required`\nAND the decision SHALL be persisted in the checkpoint's `gate_decisions`\nAND the orchestrator SHALL continue with other ready items.\n\n#### Scenario: Orchestrator never performs the replan itself\nWHEN a replan request is emitted\nTHEN `skills/autopilot-roadmap/scripts/` SHALL contain no import of an LLM SDK and no network call to perform re-decomposition\nAND the host-assisted invariant test SHALL continue to pass.\n\n### Requirement: Usage-Limit-Aware Multi-Vendor Scheduling\n\nThe system SHALL apply explicit policy when vendor session/rate limits are encountered during roadmap execution.\n\n#### Scenario: Wait policy selected under budget constraints\nWHEN the preferred vendor hits a usage/session limit\nAND active policy is `wait_if_budget_exceeded`\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL pause execution until the known reset window\nAND it SHALL persist pause reason, blocked vendor, and expected resume timestamp in `checkpoint.json`.\n\n#### Scenario: Switch policy selected when time saved exceeds configured threshold\nWHEN the preferred vendor hits a usage/session limit\nAND active policy is `switch_if_time_saved`\nAND configured policy constraints allow alternate vendor cost\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL dispatch eligible work to an alternate vendor\nAND it SHALL persist expected and observed cost/latency deltas in `checkpoint.json`.\n\n#### Scenario: Cascading vendor failures with recursive policy evaluation\nWHEN the preferred vendor hits a usage/session limit\nAND the system switches to an alternate vendor per policy\nAND the alternate vendor also fails or hits limits\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL apply the same policy evaluation recursively across remaining eligible vendors\nAND it SHALL track cumulative switch attempts against `max_switch_attempts_per_item` from `roadmap.yaml` policy\nAND when max attempts are exhausted it SHALL transition to fail-closed behavior.\n\n#### Scenario: Fail closed when no eligible vendor exists\nWHEN the preferred vendor is limited\nAND no alternate vendor satisfies capability and policy constraints (or max switch attempts exceeded)\nTHEN `autopilot-roadmap` SHALL transition the current item to `blocked` in `roadmap.yaml`\nAND it SHALL record required operator action to continue\nAND it SHALL persist the full vendor switch history in `checkpoint.json` for audit.\n\n### Requirement: Progressive Context Management\n\nRoadmap workflows SHALL externalize planning/execution context to durable artifacts so progress does not depend on one model context window.\n\n#### Scenario: Progressive context reload per phase\nWHEN a roadmap phase starts\nTHEN the workflow SHALL load only required artifacts: roadmap item, checkpoint, and relevant learning entries (direct dependencies + most recent 3)\nAND it SHALL avoid requiring full historical chat transcript\nAND total loaded learning entries SHALL NOT exceed the dependency fan-in plus a configurable recency window (default 3).\n\n#### Scenario: Learning log compaction for long roadmaps\nWHEN the root `learning-log.md` index exceeds 50 entries\nTHEN the workflow SHALL run a compaction pass that summarizes older entries into `learnings/_archive.md`\nAND it SHALL remove individual entry files no longer referenced by pending roadmap items\nAND compaction SHALL preserve all entries referenced by items with status `in_progress`, `blocked`, or `replan_required`.\n\n#### Scenario: Coordinator-backed context fallback\nWHEN coordinator context APIs are available\nTHEN the workflow SHALL publish phase summaries to coordinator memory\nAND when coordinator APIs are unavailable it SHALL continue using on-disk artifacts with equivalent content.\n\n#### Scenario: Artifact corruption detected during load\nWHEN a required roadmap artifact is malformed or missing required fields per its JSON Schema contract\nTHEN the workflow SHALL stop execution for that phase\nAND it SHALL report a recoverable artifact-validation error with repair instructions referencing the relevant schema file.\n\n### Requirement: Artifact Observability\n\nRoadmap workflows SHALL emit structured log events to support debugging, auditing, and operational monitoring of long-running orchestration.\n\n#### Scenario: Structured logging for item state transitions\nWHEN a roadmap item transitions between states (e.g., `approved` → `in_progress`, `in_progress` → `completed`)\nTHEN the workflow SHALL emit a structured log event containing: item_id, from_state, to_state, timestamp, and triggering_action.\n\n#### Scenario: Structured logging for policy decisions\nWHEN the policy engine evaluates a vendor limit event\nTHEN the workflow SHALL emit a structured log event containing: decision (wait/switch/fail-closed), vendor, reason, cost_delta (if applicable), and latency_delta (if applicable).\n\n#### Scenario: Structured logging for checkpoint operations\nWHEN a checkpoint is saved, restored, or advanced\nTHEN the workflow SHALL emit a structured log event containing: operation (save/restore/advance), item_id, phase, and timestamp.\n\n#### Scenario: Publish observability events to coordinator audit log\nWHEN coordinator audit APIs are available (`CAN_GUARDRAILS=true`)\nTHEN the workflow SHALL publish item transitions and policy decisions to the coordinator audit log\nAND when coordinator APIs are unavailable it SHALL continue with file-based logging only.\n\n### Requirement: Artifact Sanitization\n\nAll roadmap artifact writers SHALL sanitize content before persisting to prevent secret exposure in durable, potentially committed state.\n\n#### Scenario: Redact sensitive content from learning entries\nWHEN writing a learning entry to `learnings/<item-id>.md`\nTHEN the writer SHALL pass the content through a sanitization utility\nAND the utility SHALL reject or redact: credentials, API keys, tokens, raw vendor prompts/responses, environment variable values\nAND it SHALL preserve: structured summaries, decision rationale, cost/latency metrics, capability observations.\n\n#### Scenario: Validate sanitization on checkpoint writes\nWHEN writing `checkpoint.json`\nTHEN the writer SHALL ensure vendor_state and pause_state contain only structured metadata\nAND it SHALL NOT include raw error responses, authentication headers, or session tokens.\n\n### Requirement: Delegated Autopilot Item Lifecycle\n\nThe roadmap orchestrator SHALL provide an opt-in two-stage delegated lifecycle: prepare persists a batch without invoking `dispatch_fn`; apply invokes the existing synchronous callback exactly once per collected generation result with phase `autopilot`. The child Autopilot run remains the sole writer of that change phase state.\n\n#### Scenario: Delegate one item lifecycle\n- **WHEN** a dependency-ready item with an exact `change_id` is executed in delegated-lifecycle mode\n- **THEN** prepare returns a durable batch ID and request without invoking `dispatch_fn`, and apply later invokes `dispatch_fn(item_id, \"autopilot\", context)` exactly once for that generation through the bound result lookup\n- **AND** the roadmap checkpoint is completed only after a successful structured dispatch result\n\n#### Scenario: Reject an item without an exact change identifier\n- **WHEN** delegated-lifecycle mode selects an item whose `change_id` is absent or invalid\n- **THEN** no background dispatch is admitted\n- **AND** the item and checkpoint remain resumable with a deterministic failure reason\n\n### Requirement: Scope-Safe Ready Batches\n\nThe roadmap orchestrator MUST admit multiple items to the same ready batch only when their aggregated declared write scopes and lock keys prove that they are independent.\n\n#### Scenario: Fan out disjoint ready items\n- **WHEN** two dependency-ready items have valid work packages with disjoint `write_allow` scopes and lock keys\n- **THEN** both items are emitted in the same prepared host batch without invoking `dispatch_fn`\n- **AND** a synchronization-barrier test observes both host task handles live before either result is awaited\n\n#### Scenario: Serialize overlapping or indeterminate items\n- **WHEN** ready items overlap by write scope or lock key, or either item has missing, invalid, empty, or boundless write-scope evidence\n- **THEN** the items are not admitted to the same batch and each affected request carries `proof: serial_indeterminate` with a schema-valid possibly empty `write_allow`\n- **AND** deterministic priority and item-id ordering selects the first item while the remainder stay ready\n\n#### Scenario: Treat ambiguous glob intersection conservatively\n- **WHEN** two items declare globs whose intersection cannot be disproven, including `a/*/c` versus `a/b/*`\n- **THEN** the classifier returns `ambiguous` rather than `disjoint`\n- **AND** all package scopes, including integration and runtime-mirror write scopes, participate in the decision\n\n### Requirement: Outcome-Only Resume Contract\n\nThe roadmap orchestrator SHALL persist only structured dispatch outcomes and handoff identifiers needed to resume; it MUST NOT persist a child transcript in roadmap state or dispatch context.\n\n#### Scenario: Apply a successful child outcome\n- **WHEN** a child returns a schema-valid success result correlated to the current dispatch identifier and change identifier\n- **THEN** the item is completed and its learning entry is written once only after result path, branch, and loop-state evidence exactly match the prepared attempt and the resolved path remains contained by its verified worktree\n- **AND** contradictory status/outcome pairs are schema-invalid and the checkpoint records bounded outcome metadata without transcript content\n\n#### Scenario: Reject stale or mismatched child outcome\n- **WHEN** a result carries a different dispatch identifier, change identifier, or already-applied attempt\n- **THEN** the result is rejected without advancing the item\n- **AND** a resumed run can safely redispatch or reconcile the current attempt\n\n#### Scenario: Preserve a parked child\n- **WHEN** a child Autopilot run returns a schema-valid parked result for a pending gate or paused policy state\n- **THEN** the attempt is recorded as parked and the roadmap item is not marked failed or completed\n- **AND** dependents are not failure-blocked while the parked snapshot's bounded metadata (`kind`, `reason`, and the nullable `gate`, `deadline`, `resume_hint` the result contract permits — never an `approval_id`, which lives only in the supervise gate router's own ledger) remains available to that router, which is the only consumer permitted to resume it\n\n### Requirement: Durable Delegated Attempt Ledger\n\nThe roadmap checkpoint SHALL record every delegated dispatch attempt before its request is returned to the host and SHALL preserve unresolved attempts across session restart.\n\n#### Scenario: Persist a prepared batch before launch\n- **WHEN** the scheduler prepares a safe batch of delegated item requests\n- **THEN** each request's identity, exact isolation/scope/context envelope, stable launch token, marker path, attempt, phase, and prepared status are saved in `checkpoint.json` before the requests are emitted\n- **AND** a crash after preparation loses agent launch work rather than losing the identity of potentially running work\n\n#### Scenario: Resume with an unresolved attempt\n- **WHEN** a fresh supervisor loads a checkpoint containing a prepared attempt without a correlated result\n- **THEN** it reconciles a persisted host launch acknowledgement, an atomic child-start marker, and worktree Autopilot state before deciding whether work launched\n- **AND** pre-go stale claims may be reclaimed by generation compare-and-swap; after go, takeover requires positive task-death evidence, and unknown liveness becomes non-resumable quarantine\n\n#### Scenario: Reconcile lease crash windows\n- **WHEN** a crash occurs before marker creation, after marker but before Autopilot entry, before host acknowledgement, or while a child is active\n- **THEN** the generation-specific ack/go barrier prevents Autopilot entry before durable handle acknowledgement, while markers, heartbeats, handle status, exact worktree loop-state, and terminal handoff/result evidence classify the generation\n- **AND** a pre-go expired claim may be reclaimed safely, but a post-go generation may be reclaimed only after positive task-death evidence; mere absence or expiry enters quarantine\n- **AND** duplicate owners, active-lease token reuse, and stale owners that fail compare-and-swap are refused\n\n#### Scenario: Resume an authorized parked attempt\n- **WHEN** the supervise gate router supplies an `approval_ref` of the form `gate-decision:<decision_id>` for a `pending_gate` or `policy_pause` parked dispatch\n- **THEN** the resume command verifies the reference resolves to a `gate_decisions` record in the same checkpoint with outcome `proceed`, a gate equal to the parked gate (or `escalate_resume` for `policy_pause`), and a matching `dispatch_id`, then compare-and-swaps parked to prepared, increments the lease generation, and emits one continuation with the same dispatch ID, attempt, token,      1	# Design: add-live-vendor-capability-and-cost-registry
     2	
     3	## D1 — Compose existing owners and make them deployable
     4	
     5	Static lane data comes from `get_agents_config()`; CLI/key readiness comes from the existing
     6	`vendor_health.py` probe; local endpoint health and pricing stay in the dg-00 catalog. The
     7	registry aggregates those sources but does not score models or choose dg-04 dimensions. The
     8	coordinator image copies the health probe, resolves it through `SKILLS_ROOT`, sets
     9	`AGENTS_YAML=/app/agents.yaml`, and starts watchdog independently of optional notification
    10	channels. A deployment test must persist at least one snapshot, not merely find the file.
    11	
    12	## D2 — Keep four identities and location typed
    13	
    14	- `agent_id`: dispatch lane, exactly `AgentEntry.name`.
    15	- `vendor_type`: provider grouping, exactly `AgentEntry.type`.
    16	- `policy_vendor`: existing roadmap-policy compatibility name, explicitly configured.
    17	- `catalog_vendor`: optional dg-00 catalog constraint, explicitly configured.
    18	- `location`: explicit `local|cloud|unknown`; never inferred from an ID suffix or publisher.
    19	
    20	Bundled `agents.yaml` declares these values. Missing location is `unknown` only for external
    21	backward compatibility and fails location constraints closed. Catalog model membership is the
    22	deterministic union of authored CLI/SDK models and the existing provider model map; exact model ID
    23	is the primary join, endpoint kind/base URL constrain it when configured, and catalog vendor
    24	constrains it only when configured. Base URL is an additional exact constraint for local endpoints and is surfaced in model
    25	projections. This supports multi-publisher lanes such as pi without fuzzy publisher matching.
    26	
    27	## D3 — Persist availability, never pricing
    28	
    29	`vendor_probe_state` stores the latest lane probe. `vendor_rate_limits` stores bounded
    30	observations and canonical request hashes. Neither contains prices. Reads batch one probe query,
    31	one active-limit query, and one dg-00 catalog read, then join in memory. Returned model projections
    32	include catalog/model/endpoint identity, price, `available`, freshness, and staleness. Catalog
    33	misses are explicit and audited.
    34	
    35	## D4 — Deterministic effective state and model scope
    36	
    37	Precedence is:
    38	
    39	1. active lane-scoped limit → lane `limited`;
    40	2. for `endpoint_kind=local` only, no non-stale available matching catalog model →
    41	   `unavailable` or `unknown` from the catalog evidence;
    42	3. current failed readiness probe → `unavailable`;
    43	4. current successful readiness probe → `available`;
    44	5. missing/stale/no-probe-method evidence → `unknown`.
    45	
    46	A model-scoped limit does not mark the whole lane limited. It removes only that model from
    47	model-aware eligibility; the lane remains available when another eligible model remains.
    48	Watchdog persists every configured lane, including non-CLI lanes as
    49	`unknown(reason=no_probe_method)`, with
    50	`stale_after = observed_at + 2 × VENDOR_HEALTH_INTERVAL_SECONDS`. The first poll writes without
    51	transition events. Per-lane write failures never suppress other writes or legacy transitions.
    52	`now >= stale_after/reset_at` is expired.
    53	
    54	## D5 — Rate limits always expire and replay atomically
    55	
    56	POST accepts at most one future `reset_at` or bounded `retry_after_seconds`; neither means
    57	`VENDOR_UNKNOWN_LIMIT_TTL_SECONDS` (default 900). Retry-after anchors to server receipt time and
    58	all resets are bounded by `VENDOR_MAX_LIMIT_TTL_SECONDS` (default 604800). Storage always has an
    59	absolute non-null reset.
    60	
    61	SQL RPCs perform atomic probe upsert, rate-limit insert/replay/conflict, and compaction. Replay
    62	hashes canonical client semantics (target/source lane, observation ID, scope/model/reason/metadata,
    63	and original absolute reset, retry-after, or default-TTL marker), never server receipt time or a
    64	derived relative reset. Identical replay returns `duplicate`; different content returns 409.
    65	Expired rows leave reads immediately and a watchdog compaction job deletes them after seven days.
    66	
    67	## D6 — Authorization matches dispatcher topology
    68	
    69	Routes accept Bearer, `X-Coordinator-API-Key`, and `X-API-Key`. Source principal and receipt
    70	time are server-derived. The explicit `vendor_limit_reporter` capability maps to `report_vendor_rate_limit` through
    71	`CAPABILITY_OPERATIONS`; dispatcher/orchestrator entries receive that capability in bundled config
    72	and profile sync tests pin it. `authorize_operation` permits those principals to report
    73	the concrete lane they dispatched even when it differs from the orchestrator lane. Keys without
    74	that operation are denied; trust-level 3 remains an administrative override. Thus cloud trust-2
    75	orchestrators can report dispatched lanes without making every valid key a cross-lane writer.
    76	
    77	Bridge helpers retain existing `status/operation/response-or-error` conventions. Problem detail
    78	codes distinguish `unknown_vendor_lane` from `vendor_registry_unavailable`, so bridge 404
    79	handling does not conflate a bad lane with an older coordinator.
    80	
    81	## D7 — Exact dispatcher attribution through additive fields
    82	
    83	`review_dispatcher.py` retains selected `agent_id` on `ReviewerInfo`; `ReviewResult` gains
    84	additive lane/reset fields and its shared collector reports terminal capacity exactly once. Adapter
    85	model-attempt callbacks report intermediate model-scoped limits even when a fallback later succeeds. `provider_dispatch.py` gains optional `agent_id`, capacity error class,
    86	and reset metadata on structured payload/results; it never infers a lane from provider. Standard
    87	HTTP/SDK `Retry-After` may be forwarded; current CLI paths normally omit reset metadata and
    88	therefore use the server default TTL. Reporting failures never mask dispatch results.
    89	
    90	Legacy `vendor_limit:<policy_vendor>:<reason>` has no lane. It is not persisted without
    91	`dispatch_agent_id`. For that in-run policy decision only, all lanes with that
    92	`policy_vendor` are excluded because the legacy signal is provider-scoped; the skip and
    93	exclusion are recorded in structured policy-decision provenance and logs.
    94	
    95	## D8 — Lane-aware policy and request-scoped quotes
    96	
    97	A registry snapshot carries lane/provider/policy identity, location, eligibility fields,
    98	availability, and model prices. Candidates satisfy phase archetype, dispatch mode, optional
    99	capability/location, model limits, and effective state. Policy selects a concrete lane and retains compatibility `to_vendor` plus `to_agent_id`.
   100	`dispatchable` means a configured executable transport/adapter exists, independent of live
   101	availability; automatic candidates require both dispatchable and eligible availability. The selected
   102	lane writer in `phase_agent.py` carries `dispatch_agent_id` into structured dispatch payloads and
   103	subsequent retry context; initial legacy prompt-only outcomes remain provider-scoped.
   104	
   105	When structured dispatch context provides exact catalog model and prompt/completion token
   106	estimates, the quote is:
   107	
   108	`quote_usd = prompt_tokens × prompt_usd_per_mtok / 1_000_000 + completion_tokens × completion_usd_per_mtok / 1_000_000`
   109	
   110	Use decimal arithmetic and six-place rounding. Missing/stale/ambiguous data yields unknown cost.
   111	Static tiers may order degraded candidates but never populate USD deltas or enforce USD ceilings.
   112	When a configured cost ceiling cannot be evaluated, switching proceeds under the existing
   113	availability policy with explicit `cost_guard=unavailable` provenance and a warning. This is the
   114	migration from former heuristic “USD” enforcement until structured dispatch supplies estimates.
   115	
   116	## D9 — Coordinator-unavailable behavior is configuration-derived
   117	
   118	Automatic switching fails closed on registry transport/auth/payload failure by default. An
   119	explicit fallback may read only an explicitly supplied checkout `agents.yaml`, project typed
   120	fields with unknown availability/cost, and apply identical filters. Policy may use unknown lanes
