     1	## ADDED Requirements
     2	
     3	### Requirement: Typed Configured Lane Registry
     4	
     5	The coordinator SHALL expose every configured `AgentEntry` as a lane keyed by `agent_id`,
     6	with separately typed `vendor_type`, `policy_vendor`, `catalog_vendor`, and
     7	`location: local|cloud|unknown`. Bundled configuration SHALL declare location and identity
     8	mapping explicitly; implementations SHALL NOT infer them from lane names, commands, or catalog
     9	publishers.
    10	
    11	#### Scenario: List configured lanes
    12	
    13	WHEN an authorized client requests `GET /vendors`
    14	THEN every configured lane SHALL include identity fields, location, capabilities, archetypes,
    15	isolation, transport, dispatch modes, dispatchability, effective availability, and catalog price
    16	projections.
    17	
    18	#### Scenario: Dispatchability is configuration, not health
    19	
    20	WHEN a lane has an executable configured transport or adapter
    21	THEN `dispatchable` SHALL be true independently of live availability
    22	AND automatic candidates SHALL require both dispatchability and eligible availability.
    23	
    24	#### Scenario: Filter eligible lanes
    25	
    26	WHEN a client supplies capability, archetype, dispatch-mode, location, or available-only filters
    27	THEN every returned lane SHALL satisfy all supplied filters.
    28	
    29	#### Scenario: Lane-specific state
    30	
    31	WHEN one of two lanes for the same vendor type is unavailable
    32	THEN their availability SHALL remain independent
    33	AND provider-level consumers MAY group them by `vendor_type`.
    34	
    35	#### Scenario: Unknown or ambiguous identity
    36	
    37	WHEN a request names an unknown lane or a provider-only identity matching multiple lanes
    38	THEN the coordinator SHALL reject it without creating or fanning out state.
    39	
    40	### Requirement: Catalog-Owned Cost and Local Health
    41	
    42	The registry SHALL batch-project price and local health from dg-00 `model_catalog` using explicit
    43	configured join fields and SHALL NOT persist a second price table.
    44	
    45	#### Scenario: Exact catalog projection
    46	
    47	WHEN a lane has models authored in its CLI/SDK config or existing provider model map
    48	THEN exact model ID SHALL be the primary catalog join, endpoint kind/base URL SHALL constrain it
    49	when configured, optional catalog vendor SHALL further constrain it, and returned rows SHALL include
    50	model, endpoint, prompt/completion price, availability, refreshed time, and stale provenance.
    51	
    52	#### Scenario: Missing or ambiguous catalog row
    53	
    54	WHEN no unique configured join can identify a catalog row
    55	THEN the cost projection and request quote SHALL be unknown
    56	AND the miss SHALL be audited without heuristic matching.
    57	
    58	#### Scenario: Local catalog gate
    59	
    60	WHEN a lane with `endpoint_kind=local` has no non-stale available matching catalog model
    61	THEN it SHALL NOT be reported available even if its readiness probe succeeds
    62	AND location-local cloud CLI lanes SHALL NOT be subjected to this gate.
    63	
    64	#### Scenario: Request-scoped quote
    65	
    66	WHEN policy supplies an exact model plus estimated prompt and completion token counts
    67	THEN the registry price projection SHALL produce the decimal USD quote defined in D8
    68	AND static tiers SHALL NOT populate USD deltas or enforce USD ceilings.
    69	
    70	### Requirement: Fresh Probe Availability
    71	
    72	The existing watchdog SHALL persist every lane probe snapshot, including the first baseline, with
    73	`stale_after = observed_at + 2 × VENDOR_HEALTH_INTERVAL_SECONDS`.
    74	
    75	#### Scenario: First watchdog poll
    76	
    77	WHEN the watchdog completes its first vendor-health poll
    78	THEN it SHALL persist each snapshot without emitting transition events.
    79	
    80	#### Scenario: Later transition
    81	
    82	WHEN a later poll changes health
    83	THEN it SHALL refresh the snapshot and preserve existing `vendor.unavailable` or
    84	`vendor.recovered` events.
    85	
    86	#### Scenario: Probe becomes stale
    87	
    88	WHEN current time is at or after `stale_after`
    89	THEN the probe SHALL contribute `unknown`, not its old status.
    90	
    91	#### Scenario: Lane has no probe method
    92	
    93	WHEN a configured lane has no CLI or other readiness probe
    94	THEN watchdog SHALL persist `unknown` with reason `no_probe_method` rather than omit it.
    95	
    96	#### Scenario: Snapshot write fails
    97	
    98	WHEN one lane snapshot cannot be persisted
    99	THEN the failure SHALL be audited and logged
   100	AND other snapshots and legacy transition events SHALL still be processed.
   101	
   102	#### Scenario: Deployed probe
   103	
   104	WHEN the coordinator watchdog runs in its production image
   105	THEN it SHALL resolve the probe through `SKILLS_ROOT`, load the explicit `AGENTS_YAML` roster,
   106	start independently of notification channels, and persist at least one configured snapshot.
   107	
   108	### Requirement: Bounded Rate-Limit State
   109	
   110	Authenticated dispatchers SHALL report lane-scoped rate limits with an idempotency key. Every
   111	accepted limit SHALL have a server-normalized, non-null reset time bounded by configuration.
   112	
   113	#### Scenario: Absolute or relative reset
   114	
   115	WHEN exactly one of future `reset_at` or bounded `retry_after_seconds` is supplied
   116	THEN the server SHALL normalize it to an absolute reset using server receipt time for retry-after.
   117	
   118	#### Scenario: Reset is omitted
   119	
   120	WHEN neither reset field is supplied
   121	THEN the server SHALL apply `VENDOR_UNKNOWN_LIMIT_TTL_SECONDS` (default 900).
   122	
   123	#### Scenario: Conflicting reset fields
   124	
   125	WHEN both reset fields are supplied or a reset exceeds the configured maximum
   126	THEN the coordinator SHALL reject the request.
   127	
   128	#### Scenario: Replay and conflict
   129	
   130	WHEN an observation ID is replayed with identical normalized content
   131	THEN it SHALL be idempotent
   132	BUT a replay with different content SHALL return conflict.
   133	
   134	#### Scenario: Limit expires
   135	
   136	WHEN current time is at or after reset
   137	THEN the limit SHALL stop affecting availability, SHALL be omitted from active reads, and SHALL
   138	be retained only for the bounded audit-retention period.
   139	
   140	### Requirement: Authorized and Observable Ingestion
   141	
   142	The coordinator SHALL bind observation identity to the authenticated principal, derive source and
   143	receipt time server-side, and require either the explicit `report_vendor_rate_limit` operation or
   144	a trust-level 3 administrative override for cross-lane writes.
   145	
   146	#### Scenario: Principal reports own lane
   147	
   148	WHEN a principal reports its own lane and the payload is valid
   149	THEN the coordinator SHALL accept it and emit a structured audit record.
   150	
   151	#### Scenario: Principal targets another lane
   152	
   153	WHEN a dispatcher principal with `report_vendor_rate_limit` targets the concrete lane it dispatched
   154	THEN the coordinator SHALL authorize the write even when source and target lanes differ.
   155	
   156	#### Scenario: Principal lacks reporting authority
   157	
   158	WHEN a non-administrator without the reporting operation targets another lane
   159	THEN the coordinator SHALL return forbidden and SHALL NOT change state.
   160	
   161	#### Scenario: Observation lifecycle telemetry
   162	
   163	WHEN an observation is accepted, duplicated, rejected, expired, or compacted
   164	THEN a structured audit/log record SHALL identify the lane, outcome, and non-secret reason.
   165	
   166	### Requirement: Repository-Native Registry Bridge
   167	
   168	The coordination bridge SHALL expose normalized list, availability-detail, and rate-limit write

   171

   173

   176	THEN it SHALL preserve that distinct error and SHALL NOT return an empty successful registry.
   177	
   178	#### Scenario: Reporting fails after dispatch
   179	
   180	WHEN a rate-limit report cannot be persisted

   319	    async def _cost_projection(
   320	        self,
   321	        agent: AgentEntry,
   322	        rows: Sequence[dict[str, Any]],
   323	        limits: Sequence[dict[str, Any]],
   324	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
   325	        all_models_matched = True
   326	        model_limits = {
   327	            str(row["model"]) for row in limits if row["scope"] == "model" and row.get("model")
   328	        }
   329	        projections: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
   330	        for model in self._agent_models(agent):
   331	            matches = [
   332	                row
   333	                for row in rows
   334	                if str(row.get("model") or "") == model
   335	                and (agent.endpoint_kind is None or row.get("endpoint_kind") == agent.endpoint_kind)
   336	                and (agent.base_url is None or row.get("base_url") == agent.base_url)
   337	                and (agent.catalog_vendor is None or row.get("vendor") == agent.catalog_vendor)
   338	            ]
   339	            if len(matches) != 1:
   340	                all_models_matched = False
   341	                miss_reason = "ambiguous" if matches else "missing"
   342	                logger.warning(
   343	                    "vendor catalog projection miss",
   344	                    extra={
   345	                        "agent_id": agent.name,
   346	                        "model": model,
   347	                        "reason": miss_reason,
   348	                        "match_count": len(matches),
   349	                    },
   350	                )
   351	                await self._audit_event(
   352	                    "vendor_registry",
   353	                    "vendor_catalog_projection_miss",
   354	                    agent.name,
   355	                    {"model": model, "reason": miss_reason, "match_count": len(matches)},
   356	                    success=False,
   357	                )
   358	                continue
   359	            row = matches[0]
   360	            projections.append(
   361	                {
   362	                    "catalog_vendor": str(row.get("vendor") or ""),
   363	                    "model": model,
   364	                    "endpoint_kind": str(row.get("endpoint_kind") or ""),
   365	                    "base_url": row.get("base_url"),
   366	                    "prompt_usd_per_mtok": row.get("prompt_usd_per_mtok"),
   367	                    "completion_usd_per_mtok": row.get("completion_usd_per_mtok"),
   368	                    "refreshed_at": row.get("refreshed_at"),
   369	                    "available": bool(row.get("available", True)) and model not in model_limits,
   370	                    "stale": bool(row.get("stale", False)),
   371	                }
   372	            )
   373	        known = all_models_matched and bool(projections) and all(
   374	            row["prompt_usd_per_mtok"] is not None
   375	            and row["completion_usd_per_mtok"] is not None
   376	            and not row["stale"]
   377	            for row in projections
   378	        )
   379	        return {"source": "model_catalog", "known": known, "models": projections}

   190	def _weights(request: SelectModelRequest) -> Weights | None:
   191	    if request.weight_overrides is None:
   192	        return None
   193	    base = OBJECTIVE_PROFILES[request.objective_profile or "balanced"]
   194	    supplied = request.weight_overrides
   195	    return replace(
   196	        base,
   197	        w_quality=supplied.w_quality if supplied.w_quality is not None else base.w_quality,
   198	        w_cost=supplied.w_cost if supplied.w_cost is not None else base.w_cost,
   199	        w_latency=supplied.w_latency if supplied.w_latency is not None else base.w_latency,
   200	    )

   203	def _safe_float(value: Any, default: float = 0.0) -> float:
   204	    try:
   205	        parsed = float(value)
   206	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
   207	        return default
   208	    return parsed if math.isfinite(parsed) else default

     3	Provides immutable, async logging of all coordination operations.

    36	    @classmethod

    39	        if data.get("created_at"):
    40	            created_at = datetime.fromisoformat(
    41	                str(data["created_at"]).replace("Z", "+00:00")
    42	            )

    44	            id=str(data["id"]),
    45	            agent_id=data["agent_id"],

    49	            result=data.get("result") or {},

    51	            success=data.get("success"),

    53	            created_at=created_at,
    54	            delegated_from=data.get("delegated_from"),
    55	        )

    64	    error: str | None = None
    65	
    66	    @classmethod
    67	    def from_dict(cls, data: dict[str, Any]) -> "AuditResult":
    68	        return cls(

    71	            error=data.get("error"),

    74	
    75	class AuditService:
    76	    """Service for audit trail logging and querying."""
    77	
    78	    def __init__(self, db: DatabaseClient | None = None):
    79	        self._db = db
    80	        #: Strong references to in-flight fire-and-forget insert tasks.
    81	        #:
    82	        #: ``asyncio`` keeps only a *weak* reference to a task, so a bare
    83	        #: ``create_task(...)`` whose result nobody holds may be garbage
    84	        #: collected before it runs. Holding the task until it completes is the
    85	        #: documented way to make fire-and-forget actually fire.
    86	        self._pending: set[asyncio.Task[AuditResult]] = set()
    87	
    88	    @property
    89	    def db(self) -> DatabaseClient:
    90	        if self._db is None:
    91	            self._db = get_db()
    92	        return self._db
    93	
    94	    async def log_operation(
    95	        self,
    96	        agent_id: str | None = None,
    97	        agent_type: str | None = None,
    98	        operation: str = "",
    99	        parameters: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   100	        result: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   101	        duration_ms: int | None = None,
   102	        success: bool | None = None,
   103	        error_message: str | None = None,
   104	        delegated_from: str | None = None,
   105	        session_id: str | None = None,
   106	    ) -> AuditResult:
   107	        """Log a coordination operation to the audit trail.
   108	
   109	        When async_logging is enabled (default), this fires-and-forgets
   110	        the insert to avoid blocking the caller.
   111	
   112	        Also pushes the entry into the audit-triage ring buffer (D9)
   113	        for downstream LLM classification.  The push is synchronous
   114	        and microsecond-fast — no LLM involvement on the hot path.
   115	        """
   116	        config = get_config()
   117	        agent_id = agent_id or config.agent.agent_id
   118	        agent_type = agent_type or config.agent.agent_type
   119	
   120	        data = {
   121	            "agent_id": agent_id,
   122	            "agent_type": agent_type,
   123	            "operation": operation,
   124	            "parameters": parameters or {},
   125	            "result": result or {},
   126	            "duration_ms": duration_ms,
   127	            "success": success,
   128	            "error_message": error_message,
   129	            "delegated_from": delegated_from,
   130	        }
   131	
   132	        # Push to audit-triage ring buffer (D9: hot path, no LLM)
   133	        try:
   134	            from .audit_triage import get_triage_buffer
   135	
   136	            entry = AuditEntry(
   137	                id="",
   138	                agent_id=agent_id,
   139	                agent_type=agent_type,
   140	                operation=operation,
   141	                parameters=parameters or {},
   142	                result=result or {},
   143	                duration_ms=duration_ms,
   144	                success=success,
   145	                error_message=error_message,
   146	                delegated_from=delegated_from,
   147	            )
   148	            resolved_session_id = session_id or (config.agent.session_id or "unknown")
   149	            get_triage_buffer().push(entry, session_id=resolved_session_id)
   150	        except Exception:
   151	            # Never let triage buffer failures affect the audit hot path
   152	            pass
   153	
   154	        if config.audit.async_logging:
   155	            # Fire-and-forget: don't block the caller. `success=True` here means
   156	            # "accepted for writing", not "written" — the insert has not run yet.
   157	            task = asyncio.create_task(self._insert_audit_entry(data))
   158	            self._pending.add(task)
   159	            task.add_done_callback(self._pending.discard)
   160	            return AuditResult(success=True)
   161	        else:
   162	            return await self._insert_audit_entry(data)
   163	
   164	    async def drain(self, timeout: float = 5.0) -> None:
   165	        """Wait for in-flight fire-and-forget audit inserts to finish.
   166	
   167	        Callers that need the trail to exist before they continue — startup
   168	        projections, shutdown, and tests — await this. Without it a short-lived
   169	        process can exit before the loop ever runs the queued inserts, which is
   170	        indistinguishable from the writes failing.
   171	
   172	        Raises:
   173	            TimeoutError: if ``timeout`` elapses while inserts are still
   174	                outstanding. ``asyncio.wait`` returns a ``(done, pending)``
   175	                pair rather than raising on timeout, so a caller that ignores
   176	                it would see ``drain()`` return normally and believe the
   177	                audit trail is durable when it is not — the same
   178	                returned-but-unread failure mode ``_insert_audit_entry``
   179	                documents, one layer up. Raising makes the timeout
   180	                impossible to silently ignore.
   181	        """
   182	        if not self._pending:
   183	            return
   184	        done, pending = await asyncio.wait(set(self._pending), timeout=timeout)
   185	        if pending:
   186	            logger.error(
   187	                "Audit drain timed out after %.1fs with %d insert(s) still "
   188	                "outstanding — the audit trail is not guaranteed durable.",
   189	                timeout,
   190	                len(pending),
   191	            )
   192	            raise TimeoutError(
   193	                f"AuditService.drain() timed out after {timeout}s with "
   194	                f"{len(pending)} audit insert(s) still outstanding"
   195	            )
   196	
   197	    async def _insert_audit_entry(self, data: dict[str, Any]) -> AuditResult:
   198	        """Insert an audit entry into the database.
   199	
   200	        Failures are logged rather than only returned. On the fire-and-forget
   201	        path nobody awaits the result, so a returned-but-unread error is the
   202	        same as no error at all — which is exactly how the audit trail came to
   203	        record nothing at all on the PostgreSQL backend for every operation:
   204	        ``log_operation`` built a payload containing ``delegated_from``, a
   205	        column ``audit_log`` did not have until migration 035, so every insert
   206	        raised, the exception was swallowed here, the failed result was
   207	        discarded by the caller, and callers were told ``success=True``.
   208	        """
   209	        try:
   210	            row = await self.db.insert("audit_log", data)
   211	            return AuditResult(success=True, entry_id=str(row.get("id", "")))
   212	        except Exception as e:
   213	            logger.error(
   214	                "Audit write failed for operation %r — the audit trail is "
   215	                "incomplete: %s",
   216	                data.get("operation"),
   217	                e,
   218	                exc_info=True,
   219	            )
   220	            return AuditResult(success=False, error=str(e))
   221

   225	        operation: str | None = None,

   227	        until: datetime | None = None,
   228	        limit: int = 50,
   229	        delegated_from: str | None = None,
   230	        change_id: str | None = None,

          # vendor bugs, because unlike the others it failed SILENTLY.
          #
          # The intent ("text-only, no edits — read-only-shaped review") was
          # right; the mechanism was wrong. --no-tools removes READ access too,
          # so a review prompt asking pi to examine artifacts and run commands
          # got answered from the prompt text alone. Probed directly, the model
          # says out loud:
          #     "I need to read the openspec/contracts/README.md"
          # and then returns {"findings": []} in ~2s.
          #
          # agy and grok failed loudly and the dispatcher marked them
          # unsuccessful. pi returned success=True with an empty findings list,
          # so it COUNTED TOWARD QUORUM having read nothing. A reviewer that
          # inspected no artifact voting "no problems found" is worse than one
          # that errors — it manufactures false consensus.
          #
          # Read-only-ness is a property of the review prompt, not of blinding
          # the reviewer. --approve matches alternative/quick.
          args: ["-p", "--provider", "openrouter", "--mode", "json", "--approve"]
